A CAR MUST include every record in the `prev`-closure of each MST value ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#merge-rules)), including `I(C)` blocks of a page compact ([Compaction](./06-data-model.md#compaction)). The compact record itself MUST remain so the pull still proves its inclusion. Import MUST verify each commit signature and the `prev` chain back to genesis or to `since`.

## Sealed collections in the MST

Sealed records occupy MST keys. The key is `collection + "/" + encrypted_rkey` where `encrypted_rkey` is hex of `ChaCha20-Poly1305(key=HKDF(epoch_secret, "tangled.rkey"), nonce=0, plaintext=rkey)` truncated to 32 bytes and hex-encoded. Listing a sealed collection therefore does not leak plaintext rkeys. Members who hold `epoch_secret[N]` can map keys back. Knots MUST store whatever key the writer sent; they MUST NOT require plaintext rkeys for `vis: sealed`.

Public and `cap` collections use plaintext `collection/rkey`.

## Multiple identities

One knot MAY host many DIDs. Each DID has its own MST and commit chain. There is no knot-level Merkle root.


---

# 08-visibility.md

---
title: Visibility and access control
slug: visibility
order: 8
---

# Visibility and access control

Visibility is a field on the record. It is not a second protocol. Fetch (authorization) and read (confidentiality) are different.

## Classes

### public

- Body is plaintext.
- Anyone MAY fetch. Knots advertising `knot.public` MUST serve public records without a capability.
- Anyone MAY rebroadcast, index, and prove inclusion.
- Looms MAY ingest.

### cap

- Body is plaintext on the knot.
- The knot MUST NOT serve the record, its MST path, or its blobs unless the request presents a valid capability for `repo/read` on that DID, collection prefix, or record CID.
- The knot operator can read plaintext. This class is authorization, not confidentiality. Use it for data the host is allowed to see (server-side search the user opted into, collaborative docs on a trusted knot).
- Looms MUST NOT ingest.

### sealed

- Body is `Ciphertext` (or a header pointing at a ciphertext blob).
- Fetch rules are the same as `cap`: a capability is REQUIRED.
- The knot MUST treat the body as opaque. It MUST NOT log decoded bodies. It cannot decode them without epoch secrets or HPKE recipient keys, which MUST NOT live on the knot except in a client running on the same machine.
- Looms MUST NOT ingest.
- Encrypted rkeys: see [Repositories](./07-repositories.md#sealed-collections-in-the-mst).

## Capability presentation

Requests for `cap` and `sealed` MUST include:

```
Authorization: Cap <base64url(DAG-CBOR(Invocation))>
```

The payload MUST be DAG-CBOR. Knots MUST reject an `Authorization` value whose decoded bytes look like JSON (first byte `{` or `[`). JSON-in-header MUST NOT be accepted. The invocation is specified in [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md). Knots that do not advertise `knot.cap` MUST return `ProfileRequired`.

## What a knot is allowed to know

| Class | Knot sees plaintext body | Knot sees collection and rkey | Knot sees recipients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| public | Yes | Yes | N/A |
| cap | Yes | Yes | N/A |
| sealed | No | Encrypted rkey only | HPKE `enc` bytes, not identities, unless wraps are stored as records the knot can read — wraps are themselves `vis: sealed` |

HPKE wraps of epoch secrets (`sys.circle.wrap`) are `vis: sealed` with `alg = "hpke-record"` to each member. A knot that stores them sees ciphertext. Member identity is in the rkey `{epoch}-{member-base58}` — that leaks membership to the knot. Circle definitions MAY set `hideMembers: true`, in which case wrap rkeys MUST be random TIDs and the member mapping lives inside the ciphertext. Default is `hideMembers: false` because it makes debugging and capability grants tractable. Large-group MLS Welcomes already leak membership to anyone who can fetch the circle log; `hideMembers` is best-effort against the knot, not against members.

## Mixing classes in one repo

A repository MAY contain all three classes. Sync of public collections uses ordinary getRepo. Sync of `cap`/`sealed` collections requires a capability and returns only those collections the capability authorizes. A `repo/read` capability with resource `did:sol:…/pub.tangled.chat` MUST NOT leak sibling collections. A `circle/read` capability MUST return only records whose envelope `circle` matches the resource (plus the circle log on the owner’s repo, as specified in [Circles](./10-circles.md#membership-grant)).

## Blobs

A blob has no `vis` field. Authorization follows records that reference it:

- If at least one **non-deleted** `vis: public` record in that DID’s repository references the blob CID, `tangled.sync.getBlob` MUST serve it without a capability.
- Otherwise the knot MUST require a valid `blob/get` on `tangled://<did>/blob/<cid>`, or a `repo/read` that covers a referencing record, or a `circle/read` that covers a circle-scoped referencing record.
- The same CID referenced from both a public record and a sealed record is public. Clients that need confidentiality MUST AEAD the bytes and store ciphertext.

## Deletes and takedown

Three distinct events. Implementations MUST NOT conflate them.

**Author delete.** A tombstone: same `collection` and `rkey`, `body` `null`, `prev` listing the CIDs being deleted. Public tombstones remain in the MST so sync converges. Sealed deletes MUST be indistinguishable from other sealed records at the knot (same size class); the body ciphertext decrypts to `null`.

**Knot hosting refusal.** A knot MAY stop serving any record (hosting policy). It MUST NOT rewrite a record’s bytes. It MAY omit the record from `getRepo` and MUST answer `getRecord` with `NotFound` or `Unavailable`. This is not a tombstone. Replicas that still hold the commit MAY serve the original bytes after signature verification. Clients MUST NOT treat origin `NotFound` as an author delete when a replica presents a valid inclusion proof for the same head, or when the origin head still includes the key.

**Label.** A signed opinion. It does not delete or authorize refusal. See [Labels](./15-labels.md).

Takedown of public data is hosting refusal, optionally plus a label. Replicas and CAR exports remain valid. This is verifiable exit, not a global delete. Knots MUST still export a CAR of what they do host.


---

# 09-capabilities.md

---
title: Capabilities
slug: capabilities
order: 9
---

# Capabilities

Authorization is object-capability. A capability is a certificate: issuer, audience, command, resource, attenuation, proofs, expiry, signature. Tangled profiles User Controlled Authorization Network (UCAN) semantics and encodes certificates as DAG-CBOR, not JSON Web Tokens (JWT).

## Soundness properties

Implementations MUST provide:

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Unforgeable | Only the issuer’s Solana key can create a valid certificate at that layer of the chain |
| Monotonic attenuation | A delegate MUST NOT amplify command, resource, or time |
| Revocable | Issuer (or an ancestor) can publish `sys.revocation`; verifiers MUST honor it when online |
| Least authority | Resource is a DID, a collection prefix, or a record CID — not “the knot” |
| Auditable | Certificates are records; they have CIDs |

## Certificate

```
Capability = {
  v: 1,
  iss: did,                 ; issuer
  aud: did,                 ; audience (may be a device did:sol)
  cmd: command,
  res: text,                ; resource URI
  nbf: uint,                ; not-before, Unix seconds
  exp: uint,                ; expiry, Unix seconds
  pol: [* caveat],          ; extra constraints
  prf: [* cid],             ; proofs (parent capabilities)
  ? meta: { * text => any },
  sig: bstr .size 64
}
```

`exp - nbf` MUST NOT exceed `CAPABILITY_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`. `exp` MUST be greater than `nbf`.

The signature uses the Solana off-chain envelope over the unsigned capability map, signed by `iss` (or a device key of `iss` with a proof that allows `cap/issue`).

## Commands

| Command | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `repo/read` | Fetch records and MST nodes |
| `repo/write` | Insert records (still must be signed) |
| `blob/get` | Fetch blobs |
| `blob/put` | Store blobs |
| `circle/invite` | Add members to a circle the resource identifies |
| `circle/remove` | Remove members |
| `circle/read` | Fetch circle-scoped records and referenced blobs; fetch the circle log on the owner repo |
| `knot/replicate` | Pull authorized collections as a replica |
| `cap/issue` | Issue attenuated children |
| `*` | All commands; only the identity key MAY issue `*` |

Unknown commands MUST be rejected.

## Resources

A resource URI:

```
tangled://<did>
tangled://<did>/<collection>
tangled://<did>/<collection>/<rkey>
tangled://<did>/blob/<cid>
tangled://circle/<owner-did>/<circle-rkey>
```

Attenuation: a child capability’s `res` MUST equal the parent’s `res` or be a path prefix extension of it. `tangled://did:sol:X/pub.tangled.chat` is a valid child of `tangled://did:sol:X`. The reverse is invalid.

A `tangled://circle/…` resource is **not** a prefix of `tangled://did:sol:…`. `repo/read` on an author DID does not grant `circle/read`, and `circle/read` does not grant `repo/read` on unrelated collections. `circle/read` authorizes only:

1. `sys.circle` with rkey `<circle-rkey>` on `<owner-did>`
2. `sys.circle.wrap` and `sys.circle.mls` records on `<owner-did>` whose envelope `circle` matches
3. Any record stored by the verifying knot whose envelope `circle` equals `did:sol:<owner>#<circle-rkey>`
4. Blobs referenced by records in (2) or (3)

## Circle/read verification

Verification steps 1–2 and 4–7 of [Invocation](#invocation) apply. Step 3 is replaced: the root `iss` MUST be `<owner-did>` (the author of that `sys.circle` record) or a `cap/issue` delegate recorded in that owner’s `sys/id`. The hosted DID of the knot answering the request NEED NOT equal `iss`. By writing a record with envelope `circle` set, the author delegates fetch authorization for that record to valid `circle/read` capabilities on that circle.

`res` MUST be a `tangled://circle/<owner-did>/<circle-rkey>` URI. A `circle/read` invocation whose `res` is a `tangled://did:sol:…` URI MUST be rejected. A `repo/read` capability MUST NOT authorize `circle/read`, and MUST NOT cause `getRepoAuth` to include sibling collections. Authorization vectors: `spec/vectors/circle-read-auth.json`.

## Caveats

`pol` is a list of predicates. Version 1 predicates:

| Caveat | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["eq", json-pointer, value]` | Invocation args must equal |
| `["lt", json-pointer, number]` | Less than |
| `["valid_until", seconds]` | Additional cap on `exp` |
| `["max_uses", n]` | A knot that verifies invocations MUST count successful uses per leaf capability CID and MUST reject with `CapabilityInvalid` when the count is `>= n`. `tangled.cap.verify` MUST NOT increment the counter. Offline verifiers MAY ignore `max_uses`. An online knot MUST persist the counter in the same snapshot as records. Restart MUST NOT reset counts. |

Unknown caveats MUST cause rejection (fail closed).

## Invocation

A request signs an invocation:

```
Invocation = {
  v: 1,
  cap: cid,                 ; leaf capability
  prf: [+ Capability],      ; chain, leaf last, root first
  cmd: command,
  res: text,
  args: { * text => any },
  ts: uint,
  aud: did,                 ; the knot DID, or the resource DID for peer pull
  nonce: bstr .size 16,
  sig: bstr .size 64        ; audience of the leaf cap
}
```

HTTP: `Authorization: Cap <base64url(DAG-CBOR(Invocation))>`. Clients MUST send unpadded base64url (RFC 4648 §5, no padding). Knots SHOULD accept the padded form. Knots MUST reject a decoded payload whose first byte is `{` or `[` (JSON). JSON-in-header is not a valid invocation.

Verification:

1. Leaf `aud` matches the invocation signer.
2. Each certificate’s `aud` matches the next certificate’s `iss` (or the invocation signer for the leaf).
3. Root `iss` matches the resource DID’s identity (or a `cap/issue` delegate recorded in `sys/id`). For `circle/read`, the resource DID is the circle **owner**, as specified in [Circle/read verification](#circleread-verification).
4. Commands and resources attenuate monotonically.
5. `now + CAPABILITY_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS >= nbf` and `now <= exp + CAPABILITY_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS` for every certificate (`CAPABILITY_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS` is 60). A `valid_until` caveat MUST fail only when `now > until + CAPABILITY_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS`.
6. No CID in the chain is present in the issuer’s `sys.revocation` (online) OR every certificate has `exp` within the client’s accepted offline TTL (offline).
7. Signatures verify.

## Revocation

Collection `sys.revocation`, rkey = base32 of the revoked capability CID (without multibase prefix). Body: `{ cid: cid, ts: uint, reason: text }`. Signed by the issuer or an ancestor issuer.

Revocation is not transitive to unrelated chains. It IS transitive to children of the revoked CID: a chain that contains a revoked CID is invalid.

Online verifiers MUST fetch `sys.revocation` for each issuer in the chain (cache TTL RECOMMENDED 60 seconds). Offline verifiers MUST require `exp` no more than 2 hours in the future (`OFFLINE_MAX_REMAINING = 7200`) unless they have a cached revocation MST.

## Root authority

The identity key may issue any command on its DID. It does not need a parent certificate. `prf` is empty. This is the only uncertified issuer.


---

# 10-circles.md

---
title: Circles
slug: circles
order: 10
---

# Circles

A circle is a group. From the user’s point of view the operations are: create, add member, remove member, send, leave. There is no “upgrade group,” no re-invite, no new circle id, no decryption gap, and no prompt. Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) versus Messaging Layer Security (MLS) MUST NOT appear in any client API that authors or readers call.

## Definition record

Collection `sys.circle`, rkey = TID (this TID is the circle id). The author DID plus rkey form the circle DID for resource URIs: `tangled://circle/did:sol:<author>/<rkey>` in prose, stored as `circle: did:sol:…#<rkey>`.

```
Circle = {
  v: 1,
  name: text,
  members: [* did],           ; omitted or empty when hideMembers
  policy: {
    invite: "owner" / "member",
    write: "member",
    history_share: bool,      ; default false
    hideMembers: bool         ; default false
  },
  epoch: uint,                ; current N
  distributor: "hpke" / "mls" / "dual",
  ? mlsGroup: bstr,           ; MLS group context hash, once MLS has been used
  threshold: 16               ; MUST equal CIRCLE_MLS_THRESHOLD
}
```

`distributor` is diagnostic for implementations. Clients MUST NOT show it. `threshold` is written so a reader of the record can detect a non-conforming writer; writers MUST emit `16`.

`sys.circle` MUST use `vis: public` or `vis: cap`. It MUST NOT use `vis: sealed` (policy and membership grants have to be verifiable without the epoch secret). `hideMembers: true` SHOULD use `vis: cap` so looms do not ingest an empty-but-named group if the owner wants it unlisted. Wrap and MLS log records MUST use `vis: sealed` and MUST set envelope `circle`.

## Epoch secret

Application payloads in a circle are AEAD’d with keys derived from `epoch_secret[N]` ([Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md#epoch-application-keys)). How members obtain `N` is the only thing that changes with size.

| Distributor | When (automatic) | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small-group `hpke` | `len(members) ≤ 16` **and** the circle has never used MLS | HPKE-wrap of `epoch_secret[N]` to each member’s X25519, stored in `sys.circle.wrap` |
| Large-group `mls` | `len(members) > 16`, **or** the circle has already used MLS | MLS exporter secret with label `tangled.epoch` **is** `epoch_secret[N]` |
| Dual-stack `dual` | The single transition after HPKE→MLS grow | Both of the above for epoch `N+1` |

## Write patterns

**Annotation (default).** A member writes a `vis: sealed` record in **their** repository with envelope `circle` set, `body.alg = "epoch-aead"`, `epoch = N`, `ref` optional. The record is portable. The circle knot does not become a god. Other members fetch it with a **membership grant** (`circle/read`), not with pairwise `repo/read` on every sender. Cost: each member pulls every other member (N−1).

**Shared repo.** The circle has a dedicated Solana key (a DID the owner creates) whose repository is the shared object. Used for wikis, datasets, and optional high-traffic chat. One subscribe. Specified below.

Both patterns use the same epoch secret. Users do not pick a pattern as a cryptographic mode; clients pick it per application.

## Membership grant

When a DID is added to a circle, the owner MUST issue a capability to that DID:

- `cmd`: `circle/read`
- `res`: `tangled://circle/<owner-did>/<circle-rkey>`
- `exp` within `CAPABILITY_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`

This is the **membership grant**. The adder MAY also issue `circle/invite` if `policy.invite` is `"member"`. Application senders MUST set envelope `circle` on circle-scoped records. Knots that advertise `knot.group` or `knot.sealed` MUST honor `circle/read` as specified in [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md#circleread-verification).

On remove or leave, the owner MUST publish `sys.revocation` for that member’s membership grant(s) **and** advance the epoch. Revocation stops fetch; the epoch advance stops read of new payloads. A revoked member MAY still hold ciphertext they already fetched and old epoch secrets.

## Shared-repo pattern

The owner creates a Solana keypair whose DID `W` owns the MST. `W` is hosted on a knot. Records in that repo have `author` = `W`. Collaborators hold attenuated `repo/read`, `repo/write`, and `blob/*` capabilities; they sign records with their device key (`signedBy` + `proof`). The hosting knot MUST sign commits with a key of `W` (identity key or a device key with `repo/write`). That is the same hosting arrangement as any identity that does not keep its identity key on the knot.

`vis: cap` is the class for a wiki the host is allowed to search. `vis: sealed` plus envelope `circle` is the class for a confidential shared object. Collaborators cannot rotate `W`; the owner holds that key. Example collection: `pub.tangled.page`, rkey = slug.

The owner MAY instead host the wiki as a collection prefix on their own Decentralized Identifier (DID). Then `author` is the owner, and collaborators are device-like writers of that collection. A dedicated DID isolates a compromised collaborator capability from the owner’s other collections.

## Create

Owner generates `epoch_secret[0]` (32 cryptographically random bytes), writes `Circle` with `distributor: "hpke"`, `epoch: 0`, `members: [owner]`, and a wrap to the owner. MLS is not involved.

## Add member

User action: add a DID.

Implementation:

1. Authorize via `circle/invite` policy.
2. Linearize on the circle commit log (one membership change at a time).
3. Issue (or refresh) the membership grant to the new member.
4. If `distributor` is `hpke` and `len(members)+1 ≤ 16`: new epoch `N+1`, new random `epoch_secret[N+1]`, HPKE-wrap to every current member including the new one. Old wraps remain so history decrypts.
5. If `distributor` is `hpke` and `len(members)+1 > 16`: perform **seamless grow** below. This is still “add member” to the user.
6. If `distributor` is `mls` or `dual`: MLS Add + Commit, Welcome for the new member. If the new member is offline, the adder MUST use a current `sys.mls.keypackage` from that member’s repository ([KeyPackage records](#keypackage-records)). If `dual`, also HPKE-wrap `epoch_secret[N+1]` to members who have not processed Welcome.

If `history_share` is true, the owner (or the adder, if they hold old secrets) additionally wraps epoch secrets `0..N` to the new member. If false, the new member cannot decrypt pre-join records. `history_share` is an explicit policy, not a side effect of size migration.

## Seamless grow (HPKE → MLS)

The `addMember` that first exceeds 16 members MUST:

1. Create an MLS group whose members are exactly the current circle including the new member. Credential for each member is that member’s 32-byte Solana public key. Ciphersuite `0x0001`. Each leaf HPKE public key MUST be that member’s Tangled X25519 `agreement` key. RFC 9420 requires KeyPackage `init_key` ≠ leaf; Welcome is sealed to `init_key`, not to `agreement`.
2. Publish a Welcome for every current member as `sys.circle.mls` records, `vis: sealed` to that member (HPKE 1:1 of the Welcome bytes). Offline members pick them up on next sync. No accept dialog.
3. Advance to epoch `N+1`. Set `epoch_secret[N+1]` to the MLS exporter secret (label `tangled.epoch`, context `uint64be(N+1)`, 32 bytes).
4. Set `distributor: "dual"`. HPKE-wrap `epoch_secret[N+1]` to every member who has not been observed to process Welcome (initially: everyone). Application senders encrypt **once**, to the epoch AEAD key. Laggards decrypt via the wrap they already understand; caught-up members decrypt via MLS.
5. Dual-stack ends when every member known at the transition has a Welcome receipt record (`sys.circle.mls` body `{type:"receipt", epoch, member}`) **or** `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_EPOCHS` epochs have passed **or** `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` have elapsed, whichever first. Then `distributor: "mls"`. Knots MUST stop writing new HPKE wraps for this circle except as required by `hideMembers` debugging flags (none in v1).
6. Membership changes during dual-stack are applied as MLS epochs, never as a new HPKE-only epoch.

## Never downgrade

Once a circle has published an MLS epoch (`mlsGroup` is set), it stays on MLS even if membership later drops to two. Implementations MUST NOT return to `hpke`. Ping-pong is not seamless. MLS is correct for two members.

## Agreement rotation

Rotating `sys/id.agreement` (with or without rotating `pubkey`) changes the X25519 key that Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) wraps and Messaging Layer Security (MLS) leaves use. Moving a knot does **not**. Rotating only a device key does **not**. HPKE versus MLS MUST NOT appear as a user-facing “upgrade group,” “re-wrap,” or “re-invite” prompt. The rotating member’s client performs the steps in this section automatically after it publishes the new `sys/id`.

### Who initiates

The rotating member’s client MUST initiate re-wrap. Other members (usually the circle owner, on the next epoch advance) MUST read the current `agreement` from that member’s `sys/id` when wrapping. They MUST NOT wait for a confirmation dialog.

### MUST path

After a new `sys/id` whose `agreement` changed:

1. The rotating client MUST HPKE-wrap every `epoch_secret[N]` it still needs — the current epoch, and prior epochs if it retains history or `history_share` is true — to the **new** agreement key. Info string remains `tangled.hpke.epoch.v1`.
2. It MUST publish those wraps as `sys.circle.wrap` records with envelope `circle` set and `vis: sealed`. It SHOULD write them in **its own** repository so its other devices can pull without `repo/write` on the owner. The owner SHOULD copy observed self-wraps into the owner’s circle log.
3. If `distributor` is `mls` or `dual`, the rotating client MUST publish an MLS Update/Commit whose leaf HPKE key is the new agreement public key. If `pubkey` also changed, the MLS credential MUST be the new 32-byte Solana public key. Offline circle members pick this up from the log; it is not a re-invite.
4. The rotating client SHOULD `tangled.sync.notify` the circle owner’s knot after the new `sys/id` commit.

Identity-key rotation without a new `agreement` is forbidden: writers MUST emit a new X25519 key together with a new `pubkey` ([Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#rotation)).

### Old agreement window

Wraps to the previous agreement key remain valid for decryption until `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` after the new `sys/id` record’s `ts`. During that window:

- Devices of the rotating member that have not synced MAY decrypt with the old agreement private key.
- An owner who advances the epoch SHOULD wrap to **both** agreement keys if it has not observed a wrap (or MLS receipt) for the new key.
- After the window, owners MUST wrap only to the current `sys/id.agreement`. The rotating client SHOULD discard the old agreement private key once every device it controls holds the new wraps.

An offline **device of the rotator** that returns after the window without new wraps MUST obtain them from another of that member’s devices (the online device re-publishes). An offline **circle member** is unaffected except that they will observe the new `sys/id` on next pull.

### Device-key-only rotation

Revoke the old device’s capabilities; issue new ones to the new device key. `sys/id.pubkey` and `sys/id.agreement` MUST NOT change. Clients MUST NOT re-wrap epoch secrets and MUST NOT publish MLS Updates solely because a device key changed.

## Remove member and leave

User action: remove or leave.

Advance epoch. Under `hpke`, generate a new secret and wrap to remaining members only. Under `mls` or `dual`, MLS Remove + Commit. The removed member loses `epoch_secret[N+1]` onward (forward secrecy). They keep secrets they already have. There is no extra “key rotation ceremony” in the UI.

## Send

Encrypt the application body with the current epoch AEAD. Recipients decrypt with `epoch_secret[epoch]` from wraps or MLS. If a sender is lagging (still on `N-1` during dual-stack), receivers MUST accept epochs in `[current - DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_EPOCHS, current]`. Older epochs MUST be rejected for new sends; they remain valid for historical records.

Senders using the annotation pattern MUST set envelope `circle`. Clients SHOULD `subscribe` or poll each current member’s knot; they MAY `tangled.sync.notify` after send. There is no circle-wide inbox POST.

## KeyPackage records

Messaging Layer Security (MLS) Add needs a KeyPackage. A member who may be added while offline MUST publish one in **their** repository so an adder can Welcome without a round-trip. This is still “add member.” Clients MUST NOT expose KeyPackage publish, Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE), or MLS as a user-facing mode.

- collection `sys.mls.keypackage`
- rkey = Timestamp Identifier (TID)
- `vis`: `public` or `cap`
- body `{ type: "keypackage", exp: uint, payload: bstr }`

`payload` MUST be the RFC 9420 TLS-serialized KeyPackage. `init_key` MUST differ from the leaf / `agreement` key. `exp` MUST be Unix seconds. An adder MUST ignore a package whose `exp` is outside the capability clock-skew window ([Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md#invocation)). When adding an offline member, the adder MUST Welcome to a current unexpired package. The new member’s client processes Welcome on next sync. No accept dialog.

## Offline members

Welcomes, wraps, and KeyPackage records are records. Sync delivers them. An offline member who returns during dual-stack reads via HPKE wrap, processes Welcome, and continues on MLS. An offline member who returns after dual-stack MUST still have a Welcome in the log; if the Welcome was GC’d (MUST NOT before max-skew), the member is re-Welcomed by any current member — still not a user-facing re-invite: the client does it on sync. An adder who lacks a live KeyPackage MUST fetch `sys.mls.keypackage` from the new member’s repository.

## Forced-upgrade denial of service

Spam-adding members to trigger MLS is a policy problem, not a dialog. Circles SHOULD rate-limit invites (`max_adds_per_hour` in `policy`, default 30). Clients MUST NOT ask the user to “confirm MLS.”

## Conformance

`spec/vectors/circle-grow-dual-stack.json` MUST pass: 16 members on HPKE, 17th added, one member offline throughout, pre-migration records still decrypt, circle id unchanged, no client API flag. Shrink 20→5 stays MLS. Add and remove during dual-stack linearize. Agreement rotation MUST follow [Agreement rotation](#agreement-rotation); `spec/vectors/circle-read-auth.json` covers membership-grant authorization, not wrap ciphertext. `spec/vectors/mls-welcome-commit.json` covers wrapping fields and exporter parameters; RFC 9420 payload bytes are produced by a conforming MLS stack (Welcome `init_key` ≠ leaf/`agreement`).


---

# 11-sync.md

---
title: Synchronization
slug: sync
order: 11
---

# Synchronization

Followers pull. Authors do not push into N inboxes. Relays are not the source of truth. The source of truth is a signed commit CID (the **head**) and the Merkle Search Tree (MST) behind it.

## Head

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getHead?did=`

Returns `{ did, commit, rev, knot, data }`. `commit` is the head **Commit** CID (the signed Commit object, not the raw MST root). `data` is `Commit.data` (the MST root CID). No capability for public repos. `repo/read` required if the knot hides the DID (unusual; default is to advertise heads).

Clients MUST cache `(did, commit, rev)` and detect rollback: a head with `rev` less than a previously verified `rev` for the same DID is an attack or a recovery race. Clients MUST refuse to adopt that head except as specified for recovery in [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#rotation). Recovery races are specified there.

## Get record

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRecord?did=&collection=&rkey=`

Returns the record block, the MST inclusion proof, and the commit. For `vis: cap` and `vis: sealed`, a capability is REQUIRED. For sealed collections the caller MAY pass `rkey` as the encrypted key they computed.

## Get blocks

`POST /xrpc/tangled.sync.getBlocks` with body `{ cids: [cid] }` (max 256). Returns a CAR of those blocks. Missing CIDs are listed in `missing`.

Version 1 uses a **single MST**. Public collections are served without a capability. When walking a proof for a public record, interior nodes MAY mention sibling keys, including encrypted rkeys of sealed records. Sibling keys leak the existence of other records; that is acceptable. Sibling values are CIDs; fetching a non-public record CID still requires a capability. Proof nodes themselves are not confidential. Knots MUST serve MST nodes for public proofs without a capability, even if siblings are sealed keys.

`getBlocks` of a non-public **record** CID requires a capability that covers that record (`repo/read`, or `circle/read` if the record is circle-scoped). `getBlocks` of a **blob** CID MUST follow the same authorization as `getBlob`.

## Get blob

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getBlob?did=&cid=`

Returns raw bytes (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) whose BLAKE3-256 matches the CID (codec `raw` 0x55). Authorization is specified in [Visibility](./08-visibility.md#blobs): serve without a capability only if a non-deleted public record in that DID’s repository references the CID; otherwise require `blob/get`, `repo/read` covering a referencing record, or `circle/read` covering a circle-scoped referencing record.

Knots advertising `knot.public` MUST implement this method for publicly referenced blobs. Authorization vectors: `spec/vectors/getblob-auth.json`.

## Get repo

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRepo?did=&since=`

Returns a CAR. Without `since`, the full public repo (commits, public MST snapshots, public records). With `since` (a commit CID), the commit chain after `since` through head, the `since` commit block, and the MST nodes plus records needed to reconstruct those commits. Blobs are not included unless `blobs=true`. For `pub.tangled.page`, the CAR MUST include `I(C)` blocks of each compact ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#compaction)). It MUST still include the compact record.

Authorized variant: `POST /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRepoAuth` with invocation, returns authorized collections. If the invocation command is `circle/read`, the CAR MUST include only records the capability authorizes (circle-scoped records on this DID, plus the circle log when this DID is the owner) and MUST NOT include sibling collections. `I(C)` retention follows the same rule as `getRepo`. Import of that CAR MUST verify the `prev` chain.

## Notify (optional)

`POST /xrpc/tangled.sync.notify` body `{ did, commit }` — a hint that a head moved. Knots MAY ignore. Used by replicas and looms. MUST NOT be required for correctness.

## Live

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.subscribe?did=&collection=&since=` Upgrade: WebSocket.

Messages: `{ t: "commit", commit: cid, ops: [{action, collection, rkey, cid}] }`.

`since` is OPTIONAL and is a commit CID. When `since` is present and the knot still holds later commit events for that DID (and `collection` filter), it MUST send those events first, in store order, then continue live. When `since` is omitted, the knot MAY send the current head as a hello with empty `ops`. When the knot does not retain `since`, it MUST send that hello and MUST NOT invent a gap-free history. There is no byte-offset cursor. An online knot MUST persist the commit event log next to the filesystem snapshot. Restart MUST still replay `since` for retained events.

Public collections: no cap. Others: cap on subscribe. Heartbeat every 30 seconds. The server MAY drop slow clients.

## Query backlinks

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=`

Optional `collection=` (restrict hits) and `limit=` (default 50, max 500).

Returns public records **this knot already stores** whose envelope `ref` equals `cid`, or whose application body `reply` equals `cid` when envelope `ref` is absent. This is a **local backlink index**, not a network search.

```
{
  "hits": [{ "did", "collection", "rkey", "cid", "commit" }],
  "count": 3,
  "overlay": true,
  "complete": false
}
```

Knots advertising `knot.public` SHOULD maintain the index from public records they ingest (hosted repositories, follows, replicas). They MUST NOT crawl other knots in order to answer this method. They MUST NOT include `vis: cap` or `vis: sealed` records. Tombstones MUST NOT appear in `hits`. `count` is `len(hits)` after those filters (or the untruncated count if `limit` clipped `hits`). `overlay` MUST be `true`. `complete` MUST be `false` unless the knot can prove it stores every public annotator (v1 knots cannot; they MUST send `false`).

A knot that does not implement the index MUST return `MethodNotImplemented`. An empty `hits` array and `MethodNotImplemented` MUST NOT be treated as proof that the network has zero comments or annotations. They mean this observer has no public overlay (or no index). Clients MUST union overlays as specified in [Looms](./14-looms.md#annotation-discovery).

Discovery of annotations without knowing every annotator DID is specified in [Looms](./14-looms.md#annotation-discovery).

## Peer discovery

Knots do not run a DHT. A knot MAY advertise other public knot base URLs in `tangled.node.describe` → `peers` ([HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-node-describe)). When knot A first successfully describes knot B, A MAY store B’s `peers` and try those URLs for further `describe`, `getHead`, `identity.resolve`, or `node.stats`. Only the operator-configured public set is advertised. Learned URLs stay local so a peer cannot trick a knot into advertising an attacker URL.

`tangled.node.stats` is the public aggregate of this knot’s live public tips plus that same advertised peer set ([HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-node-stats)). Clients MAY crawl `peers` to assemble a network view. The crawl is incomplete by design.

## Follow

A follow is a public record `tangled.graph.follow`. The follower’s client:

1. Resolves the target DID to a knot URL.
2. Pulls `getHead` / `getRepo` on an interval or subscribe.
3. Stores the knot URL in local follow state.

The author’s knot does no extra work per follower. That is the efficiency claim against ActivityPub.

## Replication

A replica holds a copy of a repo. Public repos: anyone MAY replicate. `cap`/`sealed`: `knot/replicate` capability. Replicas advertise themselves in their own `sys/id` or in a loom. Clients MAY fail over to a replica if the author’s knot is down, after verifying the commit signature.

## Diff cost

MST diff is O(changed keys × tree height). Tree height is ~log16(n). This is the efficiency claim against Nostr’s “replay all events from all relays.”


---

# 12-http-api.md

---
title: HTTP API
slug: http-api
order: 12
---

# HTTP API

Knots speak HTTP. Method names follow `tangled.<ns>.<name>`. The path is `/xrpc/<method>`. GET for cacheable reads, POST for bodies and invocations that do not fit a query string.

Machine-readable: [`spec/http/openapi.yaml`](./http/openapi.yaml).

## Content negotiation

Clients MUST send `Accept: application/cbor, application/json` (cbor first). Knots MUST serve `application/cbor` (DAG-CBOR) when `Accept` prefers `application/cbor`, and MAY serve `application/json` using the IPLD JSON mapping. `Content-Type` on POST MUST be one of those two except `putBlob` (`application/octet-stream`) and `import` (`application/vnd.ipld.car`).

CIDs in query strings are multibase base32 (`b…`).

## Errors

JSON/CBOR map:

```
{ "error": "CapabilityRequired", "message": "…", "retry": false }
```

| error | HTTP | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InvalidRequest` | 400 | Bad params |
| `InvalidSignature` | 400 | Sig verify failed |
| `CapabilityRequired` | 401 | Missing cap |
| `CapabilityInvalid` | 403 | Cap present but fails |
| `NotFound` | 404 | No such DID/record |
| `MethodNotImplemented` | 404 | Unknown `tangled.*` method on a Tangled knot |
| `ProfileRequired` | 501 | Method needs a profile the knot omitted |
| `BlobTooLarge` | 413 | |
| `RateLimited` | 429 | Including page compact admission (`PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_OPS`, `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`). MUST include `Retry-After` as delta-seconds (RFC 9110). For compact admission the value MUST be at least `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS / 1000` (300). |
| `Unavailable` | 503 | |
| `ConcurrentHeads` | 409 | Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) `putRecord` would orphan the current Merkle Search Tree (MST) value; body includes `head` |

## Methods

### tangled.node.describe

`GET`. No auth. Returns profiles, protocols, maxBlob, knot DID, and `peers`.

`peers` is an array of absolute knot base URLs this operator marked public (`https://knot.example`). Empty when the operator listed none. A knot MUST advertise only that configured public set. It MUST NOT re-advertise URLs it learned from other knots. Connecting knots and clients MAY remember `peers` for their own `describe` / `getHead` / `identity.resolve`; they MUST NOT treat the list as trusted topology. Private or internal knots MUST NOT appear in `peers`.

### tangled.node.stats

`GET`. No auth. Returns knot-local **public** aggregates and advertised-peer topology.

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "did": "did:sol:…",
  "asOf": 1700000000,
  "counts": {
    "identities": 1,
    "repos": 1,
    "records": 2,
    "blobs": 0,
    "peers": 1,
    "circles": 0,
    "foreign": 0,
    "commits": 2
  },
  "rates": {
    "publicCommits": 2,
    "retained": 256
  },
  "topology": {
    "peers": ["https://b.example"],
    "hosted": [{ "did": "did:sol:…", "handle": "alice.sol", "rev": "3jzfcijpjiz2u", "records": 2 }],
    "truncated": false
  }
}
```

Counts MUST include only live `vis: public` record tips (`body` not a tombstone). They MUST NOT include `vis: cap` or `vis: sealed` records, capability-use counters, SIWS sessions, or any other private activity. `blobs` is the number of distinct blob CIDs referenced by those public tips. `commits` and `rates.publicCommits` are the length of the retained public subscribe log (this knot’s recent public commits, capped at `rates.retained`). They are not a wall-clock hourly rate.

`topology.peers` MUST be the same operator-configured public set as `node.describe` `peers`. A knot MUST NOT list learned peer URLs. `topology.hosted` lists Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) that have at least one live public tip on this knot (the same DIDs `getHead` / `getRepo` already expose). The list MAY be truncated; when it is, `truncated` MUST be `true`. `handle` is the first non-DID `alsoKnownAs` from `sys.id` when present.

There is no global directory. Clients assemble a network view by calling `node.stats` (and `node.describe`) on a configured knot, then on that knot’s advertised `peers`. They MUST NOT treat the graph as complete or trusted.

### tangled.sync.getHead

`GET ?did=`. Returns `{ did, commit, rev, knot, data }`. `commit` is the signed [Commit](./07-repositories.md#commit) CID. `data` is that commit’s MST root CID. See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md).

### tangled.sync.getRecord

`GET ?did=&collection=&rkey=`. Optional `Authorization: Cap <base64url(DAG-CBOR)>`. JSON-in-header MUST be rejected.

### tangled.sync.getBlob

`GET ?did=&cid=`. Raw blob bytes. `Content-Type` MUST be `application/octet-stream`. The response MUST include `Content-Length` equal to the byte length. When the writer stored a media type (`putBlob` `mediaType` query or `X-Tangled-Media-Type`), the knot MUST also send `X-Tangled-Media-Type`. No capability when a live public record references `cid`; otherwise `Authorization: Cap` (`blob/get`, `repo/read`, or `circle/read`). See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#get-blob).

### tangled.sync.getBlocks

`POST` `{ "cids": ["b…"] }`.

### tangled.sync.getRepo

`GET ?did=&since=&blobs=`. Returns a CAR of the **public** repository. There is no `tangled.sync.listRecords` method on the wire; clients MUST use `getRepo` (or `getRecord`) to enumerate. An in-process engine MAY offer `listRecords` as a test convenience; a knot MUST NOT require clients to call it.

Without `since`, the full public repo (commits, public MST snapshots, public records). With `since` (a commit CID), the commit chain after `since` through head, the `since` commit block, and the MST nodes plus records needed to reconstruct those commits. Blobs are not included unless `blobs=true`. For `pub.tangled.page`, the CAR MUST include `I(C)` blocks of each compact ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#compaction)). It MUST still include the compact record. Import MUST verify the `prev` chain.

### tangled.sync.getRepoAuth

`POST` with `Authorization: Cap <base64url(DAG-CBOR(Invocation))>` and JSON/CBOR body `{ did, since, blobs }`. `since` MUST be honored as a query parameter and, when the query omits it, from the body. If both are present and differ, the query parameter MUST win. For `circle/read`, the CAR is only circle-scoped records (and the circle log on the owner). Sibling collections MUST NOT be included.

### tangled.sync.queryBacklinks

`GET ?cid=&collection=&limit=`. Local public backlink index. Knots SHOULD implement it; they MUST NOT crawl. See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#query-backlinks).

### tangled.sync.notify

`POST` `{ did, commit }`.

### tangled.sync.subscribe

`GET` WebSocket. Optional `since` (commit CID) resumes after that commit; see [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#live).

### tangled.repo.putRecord

`POST` `{ record }` plus one of: a Sign In With Solana (SIWS) session cookie for `author`, a `repo/write` capability, or a hosted identity-key write. The knot MUST verify the record’s identity-key (or device-key) signature and MUST NOT accept a record whose `author` the caller cannot speak for. SIWS MUST NOT replace that signature.

A **hosted identity-key write** is a `putRecord` whose `author` is a DID this knot hosts, the record has no `signedBy`, and the signature verifies with that DID’s identity key. The knot MAY accept it without a SIWS cookie (CLI / self-hosted). Device-key writes (`signedBy` present) MUST present `repo/write` or a SIWS session for `author`. After `sys.revocation` of a device capability, subsequent writes that present that capability MUST fail `CapabilityInvalid`.

A `putRecord` that advances the repository MUST produce a new signed Commit whose `data` is the new MST root and whose `prev` is the previous Commit CID (absent at genesis). The request MAY include `prev` (a Commit CID). When the DID already has a head, a supplied `prev` that does not equal the current head Commit CID MUST return `ConcurrentHeads` (HTTP 409) with `head` set to that Commit CID. When there is no head, a supplied `prev` MUST return `InvalidRequest`. Omitted `prev` means the current head (or genesis). `rev` MUST increase; a rollback MUST be refused.

For CRDT collections, a write that would orphan the current MST value MUST return `ConcurrentHeads` ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#page-crdt)). A page compact that fails `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_OPS` or `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` MUST return `RateLimited` ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#compaction)).

### tangled.repo.putBlob

`POST` raw bytes, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. Optional `mediaType` query parameter or `X-Tangled-Media-Type` request header (a Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type). The knot MUST store that type with the blob when present. Returns `{ cid }`.

### tangled.repo.import

`POST` a CAR (`Content-Type: application/vnd.ipld.car`) plus a SIWS session for the imported DID **or** a `repo/write` capability on that DID. The knot MUST verify every commit signature in the CAR and MUST verify the `prev` chain from the CAR root back to genesis (or to `since` when the export was a diff). It MUST refuse a DID it already hosts unless `force` is true (recovery).

### tangled.identity.resolve

`GET ?handle=` or `?did=`. Returns DID, `sys/id` CID, knot endpoints, and `document` (the generative or operational DID document; see [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#did)). The knot MAY resolve handles it does not host by performing DNS/SNS lookup as specified in [Resolution](./13-resolution.md).

### tangled.session.challenge

`GET ?did=`. No cookie required. Returns the canonical SIWS message the caller MUST sign. See [Sessions (SIWS)](#sessions-siws).

### tangled.session.verify

`POST` `{ did, nonce, signature }`. `signature` is hex-encoded Ed25519 over the UTF-8 SIWS message. On success the knot MUST set cookie `tangled_session`. See [Sessions (SIWS)](#sessions-siws).

### tangled.cap.verify

`POST` a DAG-CBOR Invocation (same encoding as the Cap header). JSON MUST be rejected. Returns `{ ok: true, cmd, res }` or `CapabilityInvalid`. Useful for gateways.

### tangled.loom.query

`GET ?q=&type=`. OPTIONAL. Looms only. When `type=ref`, `q` is a record CID. Response includes `hits`, untrusted `count`, `overlay: true`, `complete: false`. See [Looms](./14-looms.md).

### tangled.loom.firehose

`GET` WebSocket of public commits. OPTIONAL. Looms only.

## Sessions (SIWS)

Sign In With Solana authenticates a browser to **this knot** for writes as the identity. It is knot-local. SIWS MUST NOT replace record signatures: `putRecord` is still signed with the off-chain envelope.

### Message

The knot advertises a **domain** equal to the host of its public URL (no scheme, no path, no port; `localhost` when the URL is unset). The canonical message MUST be exactly these five UTF-8 lines (`\n` separators, no trailing blank line):

```
tangled.siws.v1
domain: <domain>
did: <did>
nonce: <nonce>
issuedAt: <unix-seconds>
```

`nonce` MUST be 16 cryptographically random bytes, hex-encoded (32 hex characters). `issuedAt` MUST be Unix seconds. Challenges MUST expire; 300 seconds is RECOMMENDED.

The signature MUST be Ed25519 over the UTF-8 bytes of that message, using the identity key of `did`. Implementations MUST NOT wrap the SIWS message in the Solana off-chain envelope ([Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md#sign-in-with-solana)).

### Cookie

Successful `tangled.session.verify` MUST set:

```
Set-Cookie: tangled_session=<token>; HttpOnly; Path=/; Max-Age=86400; SameSite=Lax
```

The cookie MUST also include `Secure` when the knot’s advertised public URL is `https://`. Token MUST be 32 cryptographically random bytes, hex-encoded. Sessions MUST expire after 86400 seconds (`Max-Age`). Cookie name MUST be `tangled_session`.

### Who may write without a cookie

Hosted identity-key writes (no `signedBy`) MAY succeed without this cookie, as specified under `putRecord`. Import MAY use SIWS **or** `repo/write`.

A knot MAY hold a delegated device key and sign on behalf of a web client only if the user issued a `repo/write` capability to that device key; that is an implementation choice and MUST be disclosed in `node.describe` as `custodialSign: true`. Default is `false`.

## CORS

Public unauthenticated reads MUST send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

When the request includes `Cookie` or `Authorization`, the response MUST NOT use `*`. It MUST echo the request `Origin`, MUST set `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and SHOULD set `Vary: Origin`.

`OPTIONS` preflight MUST use the same credentialed rule, keyed off `Access-Control-Request-Headers`. When that header lists `Cookie` or `Authorization` (comma-separated, case-insensitive), the preflight MUST NOT use `*`. It MUST echo `Origin`, MUST set `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and SHOULD set `Vary: Origin`. If that preflight has no `Origin`, the knot MUST omit `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Otherwise `OPTIONS` MUST send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

Knots MUST allow request headers `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`, and `Cookie`, and methods `GET`, `POST`, `OPTIONS`.

## Transport

Production knots MUST use HTTPS. `localhost` MAY use HTTP. HTTP/2 is RECOMMENDED.


---

# 13-resolution.md

---
title: Resolution
slug: resolution
order: 13
---

# Resolution

Resolution turns a handle or a DID into a knot URL and a DID document. It does not confer trust beyond what signatures later verify.

A **generative document** is computed from the Ed25519 public key alone (`authentication` and `capabilityInvocation`; no `keyAgreement`). An **operational document** adds `keyAgreement` from `sys/id.agreement` as specified in [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#did). `tangled.identity.resolve` MUST return the operational document when the resolver has `sys/id` (or equivalent hosted identity) for that DID, and MUST return the generative document otherwise.

## DID → knot

1. If the client has a cached `sys/id` for the DID, use `endpoints` whose `type` is `"knot"`, in list order, skipping endpoints that failed recently.
2. Else if an on-chain `did:sol` document exists and lists a service endpoint of type `TangledKnot`, use it. On-chain data is OPTIONAL.
3. Else the client MUST be given a knot URL out of band (QR, follow record that includes `knot`, previous session).

There is no global directory. That is intentional.

## Handle → DID (DNS)

Hostname `h`.

1. Query TXT `_tangled.h`. If a TXT value starts with `did:sol:`, that is the DID. If a TXT value starts with `head=`, it is a commit CID hint.
2. If TXT is absent, `GET https://h/.well-known/tangled-did` (Follow redirects only to the same host). Body is the DID (trimmed) or JSON `{"did":"…","head":"b…"}`.
3. Fetch `sys/id` from the knot in that DID’s endpoints (or from a well-known `https://h/.well-known/tangled-id.json` serving the record).
4. Verify `h` is in `alsoKnownAs`. If not, abort.

TXT and well-known MUST agree if both exist; if they disagree, abort.

## Handle → DID (SNS)

Let `n` be an SNS domain of the form `<label>.sol` (case-insensitive; no `/` or `:`).

SNS is resolved via Solana JSON-RPC (`getAccountInfo`) against the Bonfida SPL Name Service program. A local `solana-test-validator` is a test harness used by continuous integration; it is not a protocol requirement.

1. Derive the name-registry Program Derived Address (PDA):
   - Program: `namesLPneVptA9Z5rqUDD9tMTWEJwofgaYwp8cawRkX`
   - Top-Level Domain (TLD) parent (`.sol` root): `58PwtjSDuFHuUkYjH9BYnnQKHfwo9reZhC2zMJv9JPkx`
   - Hashed name: `SHA-256("SPL Name Service" || label)` where `label` is `n` without the `.sol` suffix
   - Seeds: hashed name, 32 zero bytes (class), TLD parent
2. `getAccountInfo` on that PDA with encoding `base64`. Missing account MUST fail resolution.
3. Parse the account: 96-byte header `parent (32) || owner (32) || class (32)`, then UTF-8 data. Data MAY be JSON `{"tangled":"did:sol:…","head":"b…"}` or lines `tangled=<did>`, `did:sol:…`, `head=<cid>` (semicolon- or newline-separated).
4. The DID MUST be the `tangled` field if present; otherwise `did:sol:` plus Bitcoin-alphabet base58 of the 32-byte owner. The cluster prefix on that DID MUST match the RPC cluster the client is using (mainnet-beta default; `devnet` / `testnet` when the RPC URL names those clusters).
5. Fetch `sys/id`, verify `n` is in `alsoKnownAs`.

SNS seizure: whoever controls the SNS domain controls the handle, not the DID. Same as DNS.

## Bidirectional rule

Clients MUST reject handle claims that fail either direction. A DID listing a handle it does not control is a lie. A handle pointing at a DID that does not list it is a lie.

## Head hints

DNS TXT `head=<cid>` and SNS `head` reduce stale-head windows. Clients SHOULD fetch the hinted commit and verify it is a descendant of (or equal to) their cache, or a valid rotation/recovery.

## Negative caching

Failed DNS lookups SHOULD be cached per DNS TTL. Failed well-known lookups SHOULD be cached 5 minutes. Clients MUST NOT cache a successful DID→knot mapping longer than 24 hours without re-checking `sys/id`.


---

# 14-looms.md

---
title: Looms
slug: looms
order: 14
---

# Looms

A loom indexes **public** heads. It is an unprivileged overlay. Two knots can sync without one. A client that never talks to a loom can still follow people it knows.

## What a loom does

- Subscribe to or poll `getHead` on knots it knows.
- Ingest public records (and only public records).
- Serve queries: posts mentioning a DID, recent public commits, records whose envelope `ref` or body `reply` equals a CID, hashtag indexes if applications emit them.
- Serve labels it trusts, or pass through labeler DIDs.

## What a loom MUST NOT do

- Require membership for a knot to exist.
- Ingest `vis: cap` or `vis: sealed` records.
- Rewrite records. Indexes point at CIDs.
- Claim to be authoritative for a DID’s head. The author’s knot (and signed commits) are authoritative.

## Discovery of knots

A loom learns knot URLs from:

- Operator configuration
- `tangled.sync.notify`
- Public follow graphs (walk `tangled.graph.follow`, resolve handles)
- Other looms (gossip of `{did, knot, commit}` tuples)

There is no required global firehose. A loom MAY offer one for public data: a WebSocket of public commits. Clients treat it as a hint stream and MUST verify signatures.

## Client composition

Clients SHOULD let the user pick looms, as they pick labelers. A censored loom is left. That is verifiable exit at the discovery layer.

## Node advertisement

A loom is a knot with `profiles` containing `loom.index`. Methods:

- `GET /xrpc/tangled.loom.query?q=&type=`
- `GET /xrpc/tangled.loom.firehose` WebSocket of public commits

These methods are OPTIONAL. They are specified so looms interoperate instead of inventing search APIs.

`tangled.loom.query` returns `{ hits, count, overlay, complete }` for public records only. Each hit is `{ did, collection, rkey, cid, commit }`. When `type=ref`, `q` is a record CID; hits MUST be public records whose envelope `ref` equals `q`, or whose body `reply` equals `q` when envelope `ref` is absent. Looms MUST NOT invent hits for `cap` or `sealed` records.

`count` is the number of distinct matching record CIDs the loom observes (not clipped by a hit page size). `overlay` MUST be `true`. `complete` MUST be `false` in v1 (a loom is not the whole network). Comment counts are specified below.

## Annotation discovery

There is no global reply inbox and no ActivityPub (AP) inbox fan-out. A reader finds annotations on a record by **pulling indexes of records already stored**, never by contacting every annotator Decentralized Identifier (DID).

Version 1 path, in order:

1. **Author repo.** Pull the target author’s repository. Annotations the author wrote (same DID) are visible. Remote annotations are not, unless they happen to live in that repo.
2. **Local backlink index.** `tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=` on knots the client already talks to (the author’s knot, the client’s home knot, replicas). Each knot answers only from public records it already stores. Specified in [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#query-backlinks).
3. **Loom overlay (OPTIONAL).** `tangled.loom.query?type=ref&q=<cid>` on looms the user chose. Looms remain optional: a client that only pulls the article author’s repo MUST still work; it sees zero remote annotations until it consults an index.

Clients MUST union hits by record CID and MUST verify each hit’s signature and MST inclusion before display. Clients MUST NOT treat an empty result as proof that no annotations exist in the network.

Knots SHOULD index `ref` / `reply` as they ingest public records. They MUST NOT start a new pull of unknown DIDs because of a `queryBacklinks` call (that would restore N²).

## Comment counts

A comment **count** is an untrusted overlay. It MUST NOT be a field on the target record that clients treat as canonical: the target author can write any integer, and no reader can verify it without enumerating annotations.

**Computation.** For a target CID `T` and an observer (client, knot, or loom):

```
count(T) = number of distinct public, non-deleted record CIDs
           this observer stores whose envelope ref = T
           (or body reply = T when ref is absent)
```

Typical filter: collection `pub.tangled.annotation` or posts with `reply`. Observers MAY filter further (block lists, labels). They MUST document the filter if they expose `count`.

**Labeling.** Clients MUST present the figure as an overlay bound to its source, for example `12 (this loom)` or `3 (observed locally)`. They MUST NOT present it as an author-signed or globally complete count. `overlay: true` on the query response is the machine label.

Hostile looms can inflate or omit counts. Clients that care MUST verify hits or pick another loom. That is the same trust model as any loom query.


---

# 15-labels.md

---
title: Labels
slug: labels
order: 15
---

# Labels

Moderation is signed opinion, not protocol-level deletion. A **label** is a public record asserting something about a DID or a record CID. Clients subscribe to **labeler** DIDs and apply labels locally. Knots MAY additionally refuse to host (that is hosting policy, not a label).

## Record

Collection `tangled.label`, rkey = TID.

```
Label = {
  v: 1,
  src: did,                 ; labeler, MUST equal author
  uri: text,                ; tangled://did/… or tangled://did/collection/rkey
  val: text,                ; "spam", "nsfw", "scam", "ok", or a namespaced value
  neg: bool,                ; true = retract
  ts: uint
}
```

`val` SHOULD be a short token. Namespaced values (`pub.example.hate`) are allowed. Clients MUST ignore unknown `val` they have no policy for.

## Semantics

- The labeler DID is the authority over its own labels, nothing else.
- A later label with `neg: true` and the same `(src, uri, val)` retracts.
- Labels do not delete data. They advise clients.
- Multiple labelers may disagree. Clients MUST expose composition: which labelers are on.

## Knots

A knot MAY refuse to serve content it will not host. It MUST NOT rewrite. It MAY attach its own labels. It MUST still export a CAR of what it does host.

A knot MUST NOT silently drop public records from `getRepo` **because a labeler disliked them**. Filtering by label is a client (or loom) job. Hosting refusal is a different event: `NotFound` or `Unavailable` for that record, optional omission from `getRepo`, which replicas can fill. Author tombstones are a third event. See [Visibility](./08-visibility.md#deletes-and-takedown).

Clients that fail over to a replica MUST verify the commit signature and MUST NOT treat origin unavailability as a tombstone.

## Comparison

This is AT Protocol’s label idea, kept, without making an AppView mandatory to see the network. ActivityPub instance-admin god-mode is a knot hosting policy, not a network-wide fact. Nostr client-side mute lists are a subset of labels.


---

# 16-interoperability.md

---
title: Interoperability
slug: interoperability
order: 16
---

# Interoperability

Tangled is a substrate that other networks can bind to. Bridges MUST follow this chapter so they round-trip with each other instead of each inventing a mapping.

## Foreign identity bindings

Collection `sys.binding`, rkey = TID.

```
Binding = {
  v: 1,
  tangled: did,             ; did:sol:…
  protocol: "nostr" / "atproto" / "activitypub" / "farcaster",
  foreign: text,            ; npub/hex, AT DID, actor URI, or FID string
  nonce: bstr .size 16,
  ts: uint,
  attested: bool,           ; true only for activitypub
  foreignSig: bstr,         ; protocol-specific
  ? foreignProof: any
}
```

The Tangled record signature proves the Solana key. `foreignSig` proves the foreign key (or host). Both MUST verify. `sys/id.bindings` SHOULD list the CID.

### Nostr

`foreign` is the 64-hex public key. `foreignSig` is a Schnorr signature (BIP-340) over SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string:

```
tangled-binding:v1:did:sol:<base58>:<hex(nonce)>
```

Alternatively, `foreignProof` MAY be a NIP-01 event of kind `30078` (arbitrary app data) with `content` equal to the Tangled DID and `tags` including `["d","tangled-binding"]`. Then `foreignSig` is that event’s `sig`. Verifiers MUST check `pubkey` equals `foreign`.

### AT Protocol

`foreign` is the AT DID (`did:plc:…` or `did:web:…`). `foreignProof` MUST include the DID document. `foreignSig` is the AT signing key’s signature over the same `tangled-binding:v1:…` bytes, using the AT key type (k256 or p256 as in the DID document). Verifiers MUST check the signing key is listed in that document.

### ActivityPub

ActivityPub actors do not have a user key in the ratified specification. `attested` MUST be `true`. `foreign` is the actor URI. `foreignProof` is either:

- An HTTP Message Signature over `GET {actorURI}` that includes header `Tangled-Binding: did:sol:…`, or
- Well-known JSON `https://{actor-host}/.well-known/tangled-binding.json` listing `{ "did": "did:sol:…", "actor": "https://…" }` served on the actor host.

When `foreignProof` is an inline JSON object (the well-known body), it MUST contain `did` and `actor` matching the binding’s Tangled DID and actor URI. Knots that ingest `sys.foreign` / `sys.binding` for `activitypub` MUST reject `attested: false`, and MUST reject an inline JSON `foreignProof` whose `did` or `actor` does not match.

**HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421).** Knots that ingest `sys.foreign` / `sys.binding` for `activitypub` MUST verify HTTP Message Signatures in addition to `attested: true` and matching `{did, actor}` when those fields apply. Signature fields are HTTP headers on import, or the same fields stored on `foreignProof` as `signatureInput` / `signature` / `contentDigest`. Attested JSON without a verifiable signature MUST be rejected. The algorithm MUST be `ed25519`. **Content-Digest** (RFC 9530) MUST be `sha-256` of the payload body. A mutated body MUST fail.

Implementations MUST implement this covered-component set: `@method`, `@path`, `content-digest` (required on every signature), plus `@authority` (or `host`) and `content-type` when those names appear in `Signature-Input` (they MUST verify if listed). Other RFC 9421 features MAY be ignored.

Clients MUST display AP-bound identities as **host-attested**, never as key-equals-person.

### Farcaster

`foreign` is the FID decimal string. `foreignSig` is Ed25519 from a currently valid Farcaster signer key over `tangled-binding:v1:…`. `foreignProof` MUST include the signer key and a proof it is registered to the FID (hub message or on-chain lookup description).

## Envelopes

Collection `sys.foreign`, rkey derived as in [Idempotent import](#idempotent-import).

```
Foreign = {
  v: 1,
  protocol: text,           ; MUST be "nostr" / "atproto" / "activitypub" / "farcaster"
  foreign_id: text,         ; canonical id, see below
  bytes_cid: cid,           ; raw blob of original bytes
  translator: did,          ; gateway DID
  attested: bool,
  ? mapped: cid             ; CID of the Tangled application record, if any
  ? mapped_lossy: bool
}
```

**Round-trip:** exporting a previously imported object MUST emit the original bytes from `bytes_cid` when present. Gateways MUST NOT re-encode Nostr events or AT records if `bytes_cid` exists.

## Canonical foreign_id

`foreign_id` MUST be the **canonical** identifier of the foreign object, not a gateway-local alias. Two gateways importing the same object MUST produce the same `(protocol, foreign_id)` pair.

| `protocol` | Canonical `foreign_id` |
| --- | --- |
| `nostr` | Lowercase 64-hex NIP-01 event id (SHA-256 of the serialized event) |
| `atproto` | Strong AT URI: `at://<did>/<collection>/<rkey>#<record-cid>` with the DID, collection, rkey, and record Content Identifier (CID) as in the AT commit. The `#<record-cid>` fragment is REQUIRED so an edit is a new object |
| `activitypub` | The object’s `id` Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI), exactly as published, as an absolute IRI. Gateways MUST NOT invent a fragment or trailing slash. Scheme `http` / `https` MUST be lowercase; the rest of the IRI MUST be copied verbatim |
| `farcaster` | Lowercase hex of the Farcaster message hash |

Unknown `protocol` values MAY be imported; then `foreign_id` MUST be a stable, documented identifier for that protocol. Gateways that speak the four listed protocols MUST use this table.

## Idempotent import

The rkey of `sys.foreign` MUST be the lowercase hex of BLAKE3-256(`UTF-8(protocol) || 0x00 || UTF-8(foreign_id)`) where `foreign_id` is the canonical value. A second import of the same `(protocol, foreign_id)` MUST update that record in place (`prev` pointing at the prior envelope CID) and MUST NOT insert a second envelope. If the computed rkey already holds an envelope whose stored `foreign_id` differs, that is a hash collision: the knot MUST NOT overwrite; it MUST reject the write.

If `mapped` is set and that CID is still in the local MST as a native application record, a later import MUST NOT write a second application record.

**Native export.** Exporting a Tangled-authored object MUST write `sys.foreign` with `mapped` equal to the native record CID and `bytes_cid` equal to the bytes that were actually sent. `foreign_id` MUST be the canonical id of those bytes (for example the Nostr event id after the event is signed). A later export of the same native CID MUST reuse that envelope and MUST emit `bytes_cid`; it MUST NOT mint a new foreign id. If the native record has a new CID (an edit), the gateway MAY create a new envelope with a new canonical `foreign_id`.

`mapped_lossy: true` MUST be set on the envelope when the gateway also writes a Tangled application record and the mapping truncates or stubs.

## Duplicate envelopes (pre-canonical or divergent gateways)

If two envelopes for the same object were written with different `foreign_id`s (gateways that ignored this chapter, or a protocol that had no canonical id yet), clients MUST detect duplicates as follows, in order:

1. **`bytes_cid` equality.** Distinct `sys.foreign` records whose `bytes_cid` values are equal are the same object. Clients MUST render one and MAY keep both envelopes.
2. **Id inside the bytes.** If `bytes_cid` differs (re-encoding) but the foreign bytes contain a protocol id, clients MUST extract it with the table above (Nostr event id from the event, AT record CID from the commit proof, ActivityPub `id` IRI from the JSON-LD, Farcaster message hash) and compare canonical `(protocol, foreign_id)`.
3. **`mapped` equality.** Distinct envelopes with the same `mapped` CID are the same native record exported twice.

Clients MUST NOT treat distinct canonical `foreign_id`s as duplicates without one of these equalities. Merging duplicate envelopes (one surviving rkey, the other tombstoned with `prev`) is OPTIONAL operator hygiene.

## Translation tables

Normative tables live in `spec/interop/*.yaml`. Summary:

| Tangled | ActivityPub | Nostr | AT Protocol |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pub.tangled.post` | `Note` | kind `1` | `app.bsky.feed.post` |
| `pub.tangled.article` | `Article` | kind `30023` (NIP-23) | `app.bsky.feed.post` with long text, or a custom lexicon — **lossy** |
| `pub.tangled.annotation` | `Note` (`inReplyTo`) | kind `1` (`e` tag) | `app.bsky.feed.post` (`reply`) — **lossy** |
| `tangled.graph.follow` | `Follow` | kind `3` contact list (NIP-02) / NIP-51 | `app.bsky.graph.follow` |
| `tangled.graph.block` | `Block` | NIP-51 mute/block | `app.bsky.graph.block` |
| `vis: sealed` | stub `Note` content `"(encrypted)"` or omit | MUST NOT export plaintext | MUST NOT export plaintext |

Lossy mappings MUST set `mapped_lossy: true` on the envelope when a gateway also writes a Tangled application record.

## Gateway knots

A knot MAY speak foreign protocols. It advertises them in `tangled.node.describe` → `protocols`.

### ActivityPub

C2S/S2S facade over the local repo. Outbox items are public Tangled posts mapped to `Note`. Inbox items become `sys.foreign` plus, if mappable, a `pub.tangled.post` with `attested: true`. The gateway DID is `translator`. Dual-publish (a native public post also emitted as an outbox `Note`) MUST still write the envelope; if that `Note` returns on S2S, idempotent rkey collision MUST update the envelope only.

### Nostr

A NIP-01 relay interface. `EVENT` of kind 1 with a valid sig becomes an envelope + mapped post, `attested: false`. `REQ` filters are served from public collections. Sealed records MUST NOT appear.

### AT Protocol

Subset: `com.atproto.repo.getRecord`, `com.atproto.repo.listRecords`, `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` over public collections whose schemas have an AT lexicon mapping. The MST is the same MST. This is a facade, not an AT PDS.

## Honesty

| Foreign protocol | Import authenticity |
| --- | --- |
| Nostr | Independently verifiable (event id + sig) |
| AT Protocol | Independently verifiable (record + commit proof) if the gateway stored the proof |
| ActivityPub | Gateway-attested |
| Farcaster | Independently verifiable if signer proof is stored |

Clients MUST surface `attested` in UI when rendering imported AP objects.


---

# 17-migration.md

---
title: Migration and multi-device
slug: migration
order: 17
---

# Migration and multi-device

Account portability is a CAR plus a DID. The knot is a location.

## Export

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRepo?did=&blobs=true` with a `repo/read` capability covering all collections (identity session suffices on the home knot). The CAR MUST include commits, MST nodes, records of every visibility class the capability allows, and referenced blobs.

The operator SHOULD also export device capability private keys they still need, out of band. The CAR does not contain private keys.

## Import

On the destination knot:

1. `POST /xrpc/tangled.repo.import` with the CAR and a SIWS session for the DID **or** `repo/write` (method defined in OpenAPI). The knot verifies commit signatures.
2. Write a new `sys/id` with the new knot in `endpoints` (first).
3. Sign a new commit (rotation commit if `pubkey` also changes; otherwise a location-only commit signed by the identity key).
4. Update DNS TXT / well-known / SNS to the same DID (handle unchanged) and optional `head=` hint.

Followers pull the new endpoint from `sys/id`. There is no follower-move protocol. Old knots MAY 301 `getHead` to the new URL.

## Multi-device

Each device gets a device key and a `repo/write` capability with a TTL. Revoke by `sys.revocation`. After that revocation, knots MUST reject subsequent `putRecord` (and other writes) that present the revoked capability (`CapabilityInvalid`). The identity key stays on a hardware wallet or an offline machine.

Web clients: either the browser holds a device key in non-extractable WebCrypto, or the knot custodially signs (`custodialSign: true`, disclosed). Custodial signing means that knot can write as the user. It is OPTIONAL and NOT RECOMMENDED for sealed circles.

## Backup

Any replica with `knot/replicate` is a backup. The operator MAY copy the SQLite file; that is an implementation convenience, not a protocol object.

## Circle membership across move

Circle Welcomes and membership grants are addressed to DIDs, not knots. Moving the knot does not change membership. The member’s client still decrypts. If `history_share` was false, old epochs remain as they were. Device-key revocation (`sys.revocation` of a `repo/write` capability) does not remove the DID from circles; other devices of the same DID continue.

Moving a knot MUST NOT rotate the identity or agreement keys. Location is `sys/id.endpoints`.

If the operator **also** rotates the identity key and/or the X25519 `agreement` key, that is [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#rotation) plus [Circles](./10-circles.md#agreement-rotation): the rotating member’s client MUST re-wrap circle epoch secrets to the new agreement key (Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) wraps and, when the distributor is Messaging Layer Security (MLS), an MLS Update/Commit). That MUST NOT be presented as a user-facing cryptographic mode. Old agreement wraps remain valid for `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS`. Device-key-only rotation MUST NOT re-wrap.

The old knot MAY retain sealed ciphertext until the operator deletes it. Copies that already left do not come back. That is not fixed by changing `endpoints`.

## What does not migrate automatically

- Loom indexes (they recrawl)
- SIWS sessions on the old knot
- Gateway-attested AP follower counts on foreign servers (those servers follow the actor URI, which a gateway may keep stable)


---

# 18-threat-model.md

---
title: Threat model
slug: threat-model
order: 18
---

# Threat model

Assumptions: Ed25519, BLAKE3, HPKE, and MLS are as specified in their RFCs. Attackers include malicious knots, stolen wallets, leaked capabilities, hostile looms, hostile gateways, DNS/SNS operators, and other members of a circle.

## Identity

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steal identity key | Rotation keys; hardware wallet; device keys for daily use | If rotation keys are stolen too, the attacker is the identity |
| Steal device key | Capability TTL and revocation | Offline verifiers may accept until TTL |
| Hostile knot serves stale `sys/id` | Cached CID, DNS/SNS `head=` hint, replicas | First-time clients with only a knot URL can be lied to until they compare a second source |
| PLC-style directory seizure | No PLC | None of that class |
| DNS or SNS handle seizure | DID remains; handle moves | Users who only know the handle can be phished |

## Signatures

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Confuse a record sig with a Solana transaction | Mandatory `\xffsolana offchain` envelope | Implementations that skip the envelope are non-conforming and unsafe |
| Replay an invocation | `nonce` + `ts` on Invocation; knots SHOULD track nonces; `max_uses` counted per leaf capability CID and persisted across restart | Distributed knots need shared nonce and use-count state |
| Clock skew rejects a valid grant | `CAPABILITY_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS` (60) on `nbf` / `exp` / `valid_until` | Attackers get a 60-second extra window after `exp` |

## Visibility

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Knot reads `vis: cap` | Expected; do not put secrets in `cap` | Operator compromise |
| Knot reads `sealed` | Epoch secrets and HPKE recipient keys MUST NOT live on the knot | Client malware; knot that is also the client |
| Listing sealed collections leaks rkeys | Encrypted rkeys | Existence of sealed records and, if `hideMembers` is false, wrap rkeys leak membership to the knot |
| Dual-stack window: HPKE wrap of the new epoch secret lives too long | `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_*`; stop wraps after | An offline member’s wrap can be fetched by anyone with a leftover `repo/read` cap during the window |
| Agreement rotation: leftover wrap to the old X25519 key | `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS`; wrap to both keys only during the window; rotating client discards the old agreement private key after | Offline device of the rotator that misses the window needs a republish from another of their devices |

## Circles

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Removed member reads new messages | New epoch; they are not wrapped; MLS Remove | They keep old epoch secrets |
| Compromised member | They can read current epoch; MLS updates after remove | Past messages they already decrypted |
| MLS epoch skip / fork | Linearize on circle commit log; verify MLS epoch is monotonic | Split-brain if two owners ignore linearization — policy `invite: owner` avoids dual owners |
| Forced-upgrade DoS (spam adds to trigger MLS) | `max_adds_per_hour`; not a user dialog | Determined owner can still grow |
| Stolen or leftover membership grant | Revoke on remove; epoch advance | Fetch of ciphertext until revocation is visible; decrypt still needs epoch secrets |
| Malicious Welcome | Verify credential = member Solana key; ignore Welcomes not in the circle log signed by an authorized committer; Welcome is sealed to KeyPackage `init_key`, which MUST differ from the leaf/`agreement` key; adders MUST ignore expired `sys.mls.keypackage` records | Clients that HPKE-open Welcome with `agreement` fail; that is required; a stale published KeyPackage can be used until `exp` |
| Identity/agreement rotation without re-wrap | Rotating member’s client MUST re-wrap and MLS-Update; not a user prompt | Offline rotator device past max-skew cannot decrypt until republish |

## Discovery and gateways

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loom omits you | Choose another loom; pull direct | Reach among people who only use that loom |
| Loom or knot inflates a comment count | Counts are untrusted overlays (`overlay: true`); clients MUST label the source and MAY verify hits | Users who treat a count as canonical |
| Gateway forges ActivityPub | `attested: true` in UI; no author sig exists to check | Users who ignore the badge |
| Gateway drops `bytes_cid` and re-encodes | Spec forbids; clients SHOULD prefer envelopes with `bytes_cid` | Non-conforming gateways |
| Two gateways assign different `foreign_id`s | Canonical `foreign_id` per protocol; rkey MUST be BLAKE3 of `protocol`, a 0x00 byte, and `foreign_id`; duplicates detected by `bytes_cid` or id-inside-bytes | Envelopes written before canonicalization remain until merged |
| Selective translation | Another gateway; original network remains | Split view |
| `node.stats` as an oracle for private activity | Counts and `hosted` are live `vis: public` tips only; learned peers, cap/sealed records, capability uses, and sessions MUST NOT appear | Traffic analysis of who pulls stats; public commit volume is visible |
| Inflated or omitted public counts | Overlay rule: treat as this observer’s view; crawl another advertised peer | Users who treat one knot’s stats as the whole network |

## Availability

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Knot downtime | Replicas, CAR export, client cache | If nobody replicated and the operator has no CAR, data is gone |
| Blob withholding | CID mismatch detected; replica | Same as knot downtime for those bytes |

## CRDT operations

A Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) op is a signed record. There is no unsigned op gossip.

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Concurrent wiki writes silently drop a head | Page CRDT applies every signed op in the apply set (and compact snapshots); `ConcurrentHeads` on `putRecord` if the new record would orphan the Merkle Search Tree (MST) tip | Two disconnected replicas of the same Decentralized Identifier (DID) can each accept a different tip until a client pulls both and writes a merge `prev` |
