| Malicious collaborator inflates the op log (tiny inserts, spam tombstones) | `PAGE_TEXT_MAX_SCALARS` (1 048 576) and `PAGE_RGA_MAX_ATOMS` (4 194 304); refuse to materialize over-bound pages; knot `RateLimited` | Live Replicated Growable Array (RGA) still holds tombstoned atoms; compaction shrinks the record apply set, not the atom cap |
| Compact omits a concurrent op | Snapshot MUST equal Apply of the included set; extra ops concurrent with the frontier are merged on top; reader detects stale vs invalid as in [Data model](./06-data-model.md#compaction) | A replica that never sees the extra op materializes without it until it pulls the replica that has it |
| Compact spam (tiny or empty folds) | `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_OPS` (32) and `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (300 000); knot `RateLimited`; `repo/write` required | 32 new ops plus interval still let a writer publish large snapshots |
| Knot drops `I(C)` blocks | Authoring knot MUST retain `I(C)`; `getRepo` / `getBlocks` MUST serve them; clients MUST reject a compact whose `I(C)` cannot be fetched and replayed | A replica that has not merged still needs another pull for concurrent heads |
| Forged op | Each op is a signed Tangled record; unsigned gossip is not a transport; a compact snapshot MUST equal Apply(`I(C)`) | Stolen `repo/write` on the shared-repo DID can still write a compact; verifiers detect a lie when `I(C)` is available |
| Client displays a writer buffer instead of apply set `S` | Page bodies are incremental ops or a compact snapshot; clients MUST apply the CRDT (RGA text, Last-Writer-Wins (LWW) title/blob, compact union) | Non-conforming clients diverge |
| Tombstone used to hide a concurrent edit | CRDT delete is live only when every causal head is a tombstone; compact MUST NOT be emitted when every head is a tombstone | A writer who omits a head from `prev` does not delete that head’s ops |

## Out of scope

- Traffic analysis of who pulls which DID (use Tor or equivalent if needed)
- Quantum break of Ed25519/X25519 (future version)
- Legal compulsion of a knot operator (sealed records still hide bodies; metadata may not)


---

# 19-comparison.md

---
title: Comparison
slug: comparison
order: 19
---

# Comparison

This chapter is evidence-based. Claims about other protocols cite their own specs and widely documented behavior. Tangled does not win “every dimension including network effects”; it has no incumbent graph. That is stated here so marketing cannot creep in.

## Identity

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primitive | secp256k1 key | DID (`did:plc` default) | `https` actor URI | On-chain FID | Solana Ed25519 key, `did:sol` generative |
| Rotation | Not in NIP-01 | Rotation keys + PLC log | Change servers, new URI | Custody key transfer | Rotation keys in `sys/id`; optional on-chain `did:sol` |
| Recovery | None | 72h window via PLC | Admin | Recovery address | Recovery keys in `sys/id`, 72h delay |
| Handle | NIP-05 | DNS | `@user@host` | Fname / ENS | DNS and SNS, bidirectional |
| Who seizes the account | Nobody (and nobody restores) | Not the DID; PDS can takedown | Home-server admin | Recovery address; Fname registry | Nobody for the DID; DNS/SNS for the handle |
| Cost to exist | Free | Free | Free (operator pays) | Gas + rent | Free; Solana rent only if persisting `did:sol` on-chain |

Nostr NIP-01: the public key is the account; lost `nsec` is permanent. AT Protocol `did:plc`: a global directory (Bluesky-operated at time of writing) is the default method. ActivityPub: identity is the actor URI on a domain. Farcaster SPEC: FID on OP Mainnet, recurring storage rent.

## Data and sync

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Store | Relays, events | PDS repo (MST) | Server collections | Hubs / Snapchain CRDT | Knot repo (MST) |
| Sync | Subscribe to events | Firehose + pull | Inbox POST | Gossip CRDT | Pull MST; optional loom firehose of **public** heads |
| Self-host cost | Cheap relay | Cheap PDS, expensive relay/AppView | Full server | Hub | Cheap knot; loom optional |
| Portability | Rebroadcast events | CAR + DID | Followers, not posts (Mastodon) | FID transfer | CAR + DID |

Mastodon’s own move docs: posts do not move. AT Protocol repository spec: CAR export. ActivityPub delivery: POST to inboxes (N²). AT Protocol federation architecture: relays aggregate PDS firehoses.

## Access control and confidentiality

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authorization | Relay policy; otherwise public | Public repo; permissioned-data proposal is a **second** protocol, “access control, not confidentiality” | Addressing (`to`/`cc`/`bto`), often ignored | Public hubs | Capabilities on the **same** repo |
| Confidentiality | NIP-44 DMs | Out of scope in permissioned-data proposal | Not E2EE | Not E2EE | `vis: sealed` + HPKE and MLS |
| Groups | Relays / NIP-29 | Spaces (proposal) | Groups as actors | Channels | Circles; size migration invisible |

AT Protocol proposal 0016 (permissioned data): quote, “this protocol provides access control, not confidentiality.” Tangled refuses that split.

## Discovery and moderation

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global index | Many relays, hope | Relay + AppView, de facto required to see the network | Instance timelines | Hubs | Loom optional |
| Moderation | Client mute, relay ban | Labels + AppView | Instance admin | App-edge | Labels; knot hosting policy |

## Interoperability

Nostr, AT Protocol, and ActivityPub do not specify round-tripping each other. Tangled specifies bindings, envelopes with original bytes, and translation tables. ActivityPub imports remain attested because the AP spec has no author signature.

## Where Tangled is not better

- **Network effects.** Zero users at spec time.
- **Implementation maturity.** This document is a spec, not a running network.
- **Human onboarding without keys.** ActivityPub email-and-password on a server is easier. Tangled can custodially sign (`custodialSign`), at the cost of knot trust.
- **Private global search.** Impossible if sealed; AT Protocol permissioned-data also refuses this, honestly.
- **Handle independence from DNS/SNS.** Zooko’s triangle. Same class of problem as everyone else.

## Summary sentence

Tangled takes Nostr’s key-as-account, AT Protocol’s signed Merkle repo and labels, ActivityPub’s self-hosting, and none of their fused mistakes: un-rotatable keys, a required global directory or firehose, server-custodial identity, or access control without confidentiality.


---

# 20-use-cases.md

---
title: Use cases
slug: use-cases
order: 20
---

# Use cases

This chapter is **informative**. It walks applications through Tangled version 1 so an implementer can see which records, visibility classes, capabilities, and sync calls are involved. Normative requirements live in the cited chapters. Where a walkthrough needed a protocol rule that was missing, that rule was added there. Acronyms are defined in [Terminology](./01-terminology.md); the first use of each in this chapter is expanded.

Actors are named. Identifiers are abbreviated (`did:sol:A…`). There is no live network.

## 1. Public microblog

**Actors.** Ada self-hosts a `knot.public`. Bo follows Ada. Cyd labels Ada’s post. A loom is optional.

**Records.** Ada writes `pub.tangled.post` (`vis: public`, `text`, optional `media` blob Content Identifiers (CIDs), optional `reply` = parent **record CID**). Bo writes `tangled.graph.follow` (`vis: public`, rkey = Ada’s Decentralized Identifier (DID)-safe, body `subject`, optional `knot` URL). Cyd writes `tangled.label` (`vis: public`) with `uri` `tangled://did:sol:A…/pub.tangled.post/<rkey>` and `val` `spam` or `ok`.

**Vis / caps.** None for public fetch. Device key + `repo/write` if Ada’s identity key is offline ([Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#device-keys)).

**Sync.** Bo resolves Ada (handle or follow.`knot`), `getHead` / `getRepo` or `subscribe` on Ada’s knot. Replies live in the **replier’s** repo; they are not POSTed into Ada. Thread assembly is: walk `reply` / `ref` CIDs; query knots Bo already talks to (`tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=`); and/or query a loom (`type=ref`). Ada never fans out.

**Failure / threat.** Loom omits Ada: Bo still pulls Ada’s knot. Cyd’s label does not delete the post ([Labels](./15-labels.md)). Ada’s knot can refuse to host; that is not a network delete (use case 8). A client that only pulls Ada sees Ada’s own replies; remote annotations appear after consulting a backlink index. Empty index is not proof that none exist ([Looms](./14-looms.md#annotation-discovery)).

**Coverage.** `reply` is a record CID. Discovery is pull-based: author repo, local backlink index, optional loom. There is no global inbox; that is a protocol limitation with specified client behavior, not an unspecified gap.

## 2. Private circle chat (5 → 20)

**Actors.** Owner O, members M1–M19. M19 is offline during the add that crosses 16. `history_share: false`. Users add members; they never pick a cryptographic distributor.

**Records.** O writes `sys.circle` (`vis: public` or `vis: cap`, never `sealed`) with `policy.history_share = false`. Wraps and Welcomes: `sys.circle.wrap` / `sys.circle.mls`, `vis: sealed`, envelope `circle` set. Each send is `pub.tangled.chat` in the **sender’s** repo, `vis: sealed`, `alg: epoch-aead`, envelope `circle` = `did:sol:O…#<circle-rkey>`. On add, O issues a **membership grant**: `circle/read` on `tangled://circle/did:sol:O…/<rkey>` to the new member ([Circles](./10-circles.md#membership-grant), [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md)).

**Vis / caps.** Fetch: `circle/read` (cross-repo) or `repo/read` on the sender. Read: `epoch_secret[N]`. The hosting knot sees ciphertext and, unless `hideMembers`, wrap rkeys.

**Sync.** Members list peers from `sys.circle`, resolve each `sys/id`, `getRepoAuth` / `subscribe` with `circle/read`. Annotation pattern: N−1 pulls. Crossing 16 is still “add member”: same circle id, dual-stack epoch, Welcomes in the log. M19 returns, reads via wrap, processes Welcome, continues. Pre-join records do not decrypt (`history_share` false). Shrink 20→5 stays on the large-group distributor ([Circles](./10-circles.md#never-downgrade)).

**Failure / threat.** Removed member keeps old epochs, loses new ones. Forced adds are rate-limited, not a confirm dialog. Offline past dual-stack max-skew: client re-Welcomes on sync; not a user-facing re-invite. Honest loss: membership grants must be revoked on remove or the removed member can still **fetch** ciphertext they can no longer decrypt.

**Coverage.** Size migration was specified. Missing pieces were envelope `circle`, `circle/read`, and how members fetch each other’s annotation-pattern messages.

## 3. Long-form publishing with media and comments

**Actors.** Ada publishes. Bo comments. Media on Ada’s knot.

**Records.** Ada `putBlob` for the article body (markdown) and for images. Ada writes `pub.tangled.media` (`blob`, `mime`, `alt`) and `pub.tangled.article` (`title`, `blob` canonical body, optional `text` preview, `media` CIDs). Bo writes `pub.tangled.annotation` in Bo’s repo with envelope `ref` = article CID.

**Vis / caps.** Public article: anyone `getRecord` / `getBlob`. Capability-gated draft: `vis: cap` until Ada writes a public successor (`prev`).

**Sync.** Readers pull Ada. Comments: pull Bo if known; `tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=<article>` on knots already in use; optional loom `type=ref&q=<article-cid>`. Counts from those queries are overlays (`overlay: true`), never a field Ada can forge as canonical ([Looms](./14-looms.md#comment-counts)). Blobs via `tangled.sync.getBlob` ([Synchronization](./11-sync.md#get-blob)).

**Failure / threat.** Ada tombstones the article; blob becomes non-public once no live public record references it. Bo’s annotation remains in Bo’s repo (dangling `ref` is allowed). A client that never consults an index sees zero remote comments; that is required behavior, not a bug.

**Coverage.** Article schema, `pub.tangled.annotation`, `ref`, `getBlob`, backlink query, overlay counts.

## 4. Shared wiki / dataset (shared-repo)

**Actors.** Owner O creates circle DID `did:sol:W…` (dedicated key) hosted on O’s knot. Collaborators C1, C2.

**Records.** Circle definition as in use case 2. Wiki pages: `pub.tangled.page` in **W’s** Merkle Search Tree (MST), rkey = slug (`Home`, `rfc.draft` displayed as `rfc/draft`). Dataset rows: application collection plus blobs. Concurrent page edits: Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) — Replicated Growable Array (RGA) on `text`, Last-Writer-Wins (LWW) registers on `title` and `blob`. Two writers who have not seen each other both keep their inserts; apply order does not pick a whole-page winner. A later compact is a signed snapshot of that apply at a frontier of included op CIDs; a late op concurrent with the compact still applies on top ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#page-crdt), [Compaction](./06-data-model.md#compaction)). Posts and annotations stay Last-ts-wins and do not compact. Slugs MUST NOT contain `/`; `.` is the nested-page separator ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#page-slugs)).

**Vis / caps.** Typical wiki: `vis: cap` (host may search). Confidential wiki: `vis: sealed` + envelope `circle` + epoch Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD). O issues to each collaborator: `repo/read` + `repo/write` + `blob/*` attenuated to `tangled://did:sol:W…/pub.tangled.page` (and blob prefix), plus `circle/read` if sealed. Writers sign records with their device key; `author` is `did:sol:W…`; `signedBy` + `proof` required. The knot signs **commits** with a device key of W ([Circles](./10-circles.md#shared-repo-pattern)).

**Sync.** One `subscribe` on W. Not N member pulls.

**Failure / threat.** `vis: cap` means O’s knot operator can read plaintext — that is the point of this class. Stolen collaborator cap: revoke, epoch-advance if sealed. The circle identity key is another secret O must hold; collaborators cannot rotate W. Compact spam is knot-rate-limited. A compact that missed a concurrent edit is stale: clients that have the extra op merge it; they do not drop it.

**Coverage.** Shared-repo pattern, commit signing, `author`/`signedBy`, page CRDT, compaction, nested slugs. Last-ts-wins remains for posts, annotations, and graph keys.

## 5. Cross-network import, export, dual-publish

**Actors.** Gateway G (`gateway.nostr` + `gateway.ap`). Ada bound to a Nostr key (verifiable) and an ActivityPub (AP) actor (attested).

**Records.** `sys.binding` for each foreign id. Import: blob of original bytes; `sys.foreign` with canonical `foreign_id` (Nostr event id, AT strong URI, ActivityPub object `id` Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI), Farcaster message hash), `bytes_cid`, `translator` = G, `attested` false for Nostr and true for AP; optional mapped `pub.tangled.post`. rkey of `sys.foreign` MUST be hex of BLAKE3 (`protocol || 0x00 || canonical foreign_id`) ([Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md#canonical-foreign_id)).

**Round-trip.** Export MUST emit `bytes_cid` bytes when present. Native Ada post exported to Nostr: G writes `sys.foreign` with `mapped` = Ada’s post CID and `bytes_cid` = the event bytes. Re-export of that CID MUST reuse the envelope and MUST NOT mint a new event id. Re-import MUST NOT create a second post. If two gateways used different `foreign_id`s before canonicalization, clients detect duplicates by `bytes_cid` equality or the protocol id inside the bytes.

**Dual-publish.** Ada’s public post is mapped to an AP `Note` in G’s outbox. If that `Note` returns on Server-to-Server (S2S), the idempotent envelope key collides and G updates the envelope, not the native record.

**Failure / threat.** Clients MUST show AP objects as host-attested. G can lie about AP; G cannot forge a Nostr sig if the client verifies. AP follower counts live on foreign servers; article→Authenticated Transfer Protocol (ATProto) is lossy (`mapped_lossy`).

**Coverage.** Bindings, envelopes, attested vs verifiable, canonical `foreign_id`, idempotent rkeys, native-export `mapped`, duplicate detection.

## 6. Account migration

**Actors.** Ada moves from knot K1 to K2. Same DID, same handle. Laptop device key revoked. Circle member throughout.

**Records.** Export a Content Addressable aRchive (CAR) (`getRepo?blobs=true` with a cap covering all classes). `import` on K2. New `sys/id` with K2 first in `endpoints`. Location commit (identity key). Domain Name System (DNS) / Solana Name Service (SNS) unchanged for the DID; update knot URL / `head=` hint. `sys.revocation` for the laptop capability.

**Vis / caps.** Identity session on K2. Membership grants are to Ada’s DID, not K1; circle membership survives ([Migration](./17-migration.md)). Device revoke does not remove Ada from circles.

**Sync.** Followers re-resolve `sys/id` (max 24h cache). K1 MAY 301 `getHead`. No follower-move protocol.

**Failure / threat.** Sign In With Solana (SIWS) on K1 dies. Looms recrawl. K1 may still hold sealed ciphertext until the operator deletes it; copies that left K1 remain. If nobody replicated and the CAR is lost, data is gone. **Location move does not rotate keys.** If Ada also rotates the identity and agreement keys, her client MUST re-wrap circle epoch secrets to the new X25519 `agreement` key (and MLS-Update if the circle is on MLS) without a user-facing mode ([Circles](./10-circles.md#agreement-rotation), [Migration](./17-migration.md#circle-membership-across-move)). Device-key-only revoke of the laptop does not re-wrap.

**Coverage.** Location vs identity rotation vs device rotation are distinct. Foreign AP followers follow G’s actor URI, not K1.

## 7. Sealed media album (invented)

**Actors.** Ada shares an album with circle C (use case 2), not with the public.

**Records.** For each photo: AEAD the bytes under `epoch_secret[N]`; `putBlob` the ciphertext; `pub.tangled.media` with `vis: sealed`, envelope `circle`, `Ciphertext` header `{alg: epoch-aead, epoch: N, blob: cid}` (`ct` omitted). Album index: `pub.tangled.album` (`title`, `items` = media record CIDs), same vis and `circle`.

**Vis / caps.** `circle/read` + `blob/get` (implied by `circle/read` for referenced blobs). Knot MUST NOT serve these blobs as public. Clients MUST encrypt media bytes; a plaintext blob CID in a sealed body is fetchable by anyone who learns the CID from a leak.

**Sync.** Members pull Ada (and other contributors) as in use case 2; `getBlob` per item.

**Failure / threat.** `history_share: false`: a late joiner does not decrypt old photos. Removed member keeps photos they already fetched. Same CID placed in a **public** record makes the bytes public. Honest loss: encrypted rkeys hide names, not the count of sealed objects on the knot.

**Coverage.** Ciphertext-as-blob existed; `getBlob` authorization and the album schema did not.

## 8. Takedown versus replica (invented)

**Actors.** Ada’s public post. Knot K refuses to keep hosting it (policy). Replica R still has the CAR. Labeler L writes `val: nsfw`.

**Records.** Three different objects, not one:

| Event | What the MST does | What clients see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Author delete | Tombstone (`body` `null`, `prev` set) | Protocol delete; sync converges |
| Knot hosting refusal | Bytes unchanged if retained; MAY omit from `getRepo` | `NotFound` or `Unavailable`; **not** a tombstone |
| Label | New `tangled.label` | Opinion; compose labelers |

**Sync.** Clients that only talk to K lose availability. Clients that fail over to R, after verifying commit signatures, still see the post unless Ada tombstoned it. K MUST NOT rewrite record bytes.

**Failure / threat.** Users confuse K’s 404 with Ada’s delete. Hostile K withholds; replicas detect by head/rev, not by filling missing records as “deleted.” Honest loss: there is no global takedown.

**Coverage.** Visibility and labels said this in outline; the three-way distinction and replica failover were easy to misread.


---

# 21-changelog.md

---
title: Changelog
slug: changelog
order: 21
---

# Changelog

This chapter records **normative** protocol changes shipped after the first complete v1 draft. It is not a client or product changelog. Informal names in parentheses are not wire identifiers.

Each item states the problem, the change, and the RFC 2119 language. Implementers who already shipped an earlier v1 snapshot MUST apply these rules; `v` on records, commits, and capabilities remains `1`.

## 21.1 Credentialed Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) preflight

**Problem.** Actual responses already echo `Origin` and send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` when `Cookie` or `Authorization` is present. `OPTIONS` always sent `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so browsers rejected credentialed preflight.

**Change.** Preflight uses the same credentialed rule as the actual response, keyed off `Access-Control-Request-Headers`.

A knot MUST send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on `OPTIONS` when `Access-Control-Request-Headers` does not list `Cookie` or `Authorization`.

When `Access-Control-Request-Headers` lists `Cookie` or `Authorization` (comma-separated, case-insensitive), the `OPTIONS` response MUST NOT use `*`. It MUST echo the request `Origin`, MUST set `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and SHOULD set `Vary: Origin`. If that preflight has no `Origin`, the knot MUST omit `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#cors).

## 21.2 Capability `max_uses` counted

**Problem.** Spec 09 listed `["max_uses", n]` but said a knot MAY skip the counter. The reference knot skipped it, so a one-use grant was reusable.

**Change.** Online knots that accept invocations MUST count successful uses per leaf capability Content Identifier (CID).

A knot that verifies invocations MUST persist a counter keyed by the leaf capability CID. Before authorizing, it MUST reject the invocation with `CapabilityInvalid` (HTTP 403) if the stored count is greater than or equal to `n`. After a successful authorization it MUST increment the counter.

`tangled.cap.verify` MUST NOT increment the counter (it is a check, not a resource use). Offline verifiers MAY ignore `max_uses`. Online knots persist the counter; see [21.18](#2118-max_uses-persisted-across-restart).

See [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md#caveats).

## 21.3 `listRecords` is not on the wire

**Problem.** The in-process engine served `GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.listRecords`. OpenAPI omitted it. Spec 12 already forbade a wire method. Live knots still answered the path.

**Change.** Confirm the forbid. Clients MUST enumerate with `getRepo`, `getRepoAuth`, or `getRecord`.

A Tangled knot MUST return `MethodNotImplemented` (HTTP 404) for `tangled.sync.listRecords`. An in-process engine MAY keep a `listRecords` helper for tests. A knot MUST NOT require clients to call it.

See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-sync-getrepo).

## 21.4 `getRepoAuth` `since` in query or body

**Problem.** Spec 12 already allowed `since` as a query parameter or in the JSON/CBOR body. The reference knot read only the query string.

**Change.** Honor both. If both are present and differ, the query parameter MUST win.

A knot MUST treat `since` on `tangled.sync.getRepoAuth` as a commit or record CID. It MUST read `since` from the query string when present. If the query omits `since`, it MUST read `since` from the request body when present.

See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-sync-getrepoauth).

## 21.5 KeyPackage records for offline add

**Problem.** Messaging Layer Security (MLS) Add needs a KeyPackage. Spec 10 published Welcomes for offline members but did not say how an adder obtains a KeyPackage when the new member is offline. That forced a round-trip or an out-of-band package.

**Change.** Members publish KeyPackage records in their own repository. Add is still “add member.” Clients MUST NOT expose Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) versus MLS, or KeyPackage publish, as a user-facing mode.

A `client.group` implementation MUST be able to publish a KeyPackage record:

- collection `sys.mls.keypackage`
- rkey = a Timestamp Identifier (TID)
- `vis` `public` or `cap`
- body `{ type: "keypackage", exp: uint, payload: bstr }`

`payload` MUST be the RFC 9420 TLS-serialized KeyPackage. `init_key` MUST differ from the leaf / `agreement` key. `exp` MUST be Unix seconds. An adder MUST ignore a package with `exp` less than now (the [clock-skew window](#216-capability-clock-skew) applies). An adder MUST Welcome to a current unexpired package when adding an offline member. The new member’s client processes Welcome on next sync. No accept dialog.

See [Circles](./10-circles.md#keypackage-records).

## 21.6 Subscribe `since` cursor

**Problem.** Spec 11 live subscribe had no resume cursor. A dropped WebSocket forced a full `getRepo` before the client could trust it had not missed a commit.

**Change.** Optional `since` query parameter (a commit CID).

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.subscribe?did=&collection=&since=` — `since` is OPTIONAL. When `since` is present and the knot still holds later commit events for that Decentralized Identifier (DID) (and `collection` filter), it MUST send those events first, in store order, then continue live. When `since` is omitted, the knot MAY send the current head as a hello with empty `ops` (v1 default). When the knot does not retain `since`, it MUST send that hello and MUST NOT invent a gap-free history.

Subscribe filters remain `did` and optional `collection`. There is no byte-offset cursor. The event log is persisted; see [21.14](#2114-subscribe-since-persisted).

See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#live).

## 21.7 Blob size and media type on `getBlob`

**Problem.** `putBlob` accepted raw bytes. `getBlob` returned `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` with no size or stored type, so clients could not advertise media without out-of-band metadata.

**Change.** Always send length. Echo a stored type when the writer supplied one.

`putBlob` MAY include `mediaType` as a query parameter or `X-Tangled-Media-Type` request header (a Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type such as `image/png`). The body `Content-Type` remains `application/octet-stream`. A knot MUST store that type with the blob when present.

`getBlob` MUST send `Content-Length` equal to the byte length. `Content-Type` MUST remain `application/octet-stream` (the CID is raw 0x55). When a media type was stored, the knot MUST also send `X-Tangled-Media-Type` with that value.

See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-sync-getblob).

## 21.8 Capability clock-skew window

**Problem.** Capability `nbf` already existed. Verifiers compared `nbf` and `exp` to `now` with no skew, so a 1-second clock difference rejected a valid grant.

**Change.** A 60-second window on not-before, expiry, and `valid_until`.

Let `SKEW` be `CAPABILITY_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS` (60). A verifier MUST accept a certificate when `now + SKEW >= nbf` and `now <= exp + SKEW`. A `valid_until` caveat MUST fail only when `now > until + SKEW`. Implementations MUST use 60. They MUST NOT expose the window as an interop-breaking setting.

See [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md#invocation) and [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md#constants).

## 21.9 `Retry-After` on `RateLimited`

**Problem.** Page compact admission already returned `RateLimited` (HTTP 429) with no `Retry-After`, so clients could not back off correctly.

**Change.** Every `RateLimited` response MUST include `Retry-After` as delta-seconds (RFC 9110). For page compact admission the value MUST be at least `PAGE_COMPACT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS / 1000` (300).

See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#errors).

## 21.10 Generative vs operational DID `keyAgreement`

**Problem.** A generative `did:sol` document is computed from the Ed25519 public key alone. Putting X25519 on that document would require deriving agreement from the identity key (forbidden) or fetching `sys/id` (not generative). Resolvers had no `keyAgreement` even after `sys/id` was published.

**Change.** Split the document. The generative document MUST NOT include `keyAgreement`. The operational document MUST include `keyAgreement` for `sys/id.agreement` when that record is available.

A generative document MUST grant `authentication` and `capabilityInvocation` to the 32-byte Ed25519 key and MUST NOT invent `keyAgreement`. Implementations MUST NOT convert the identity Ed25519 key to X25519 for Diffie–Hellman.

When a knot or client has `sys/id` (or equivalent hosted identity), `tangled.identity.resolve` and any `did:sol` document builder MUST return the operational document: the generative methods plus `keyAgreement` with id `did:sol:<base58>#agreement`, type `X25519KeyAgreementKey2020`, and `publicKeyBase58` of the X25519 `agreement` public key. Without `sys/id`, they MUST return the generative document.

See [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#did) and [Resolution](./13-resolution.md).

## 21.11 HTTP Message Signatures on ActivityPub import

**Problem.** ActivityPub imports required `attested: true` and matching well-known JSON `{did, actor}`. HTTP Message Signature headers on the foreign payload were not verified, so a mutated body could still be stored if the JSON proof matched.

**Change.** Keep the attestation rule. Verify RFC 9421 when signature fields are present.

Knots that ingest `sys.foreign` / `sys.binding` for `activitypub` MUST reject `attested: false`. Matching inline JSON `{did, actor}` remains REQUIRED when those fields are present. RFC 9421 is now required, not optional; see [21.16](#2116-activitypub-rfc-9421-required).

See [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md#activitypub).

## 21.12 Signed Commit `prev` chain on `putRecord`

**Problem.** The reference knot advertised `getHead.commit` as the Merkle Search Tree (MST) root CID. Spec 07 already defined a signed Commit `{ did, version, data, prev, rev, sig }`. Import could not verify a commit chain.

**Change.** `putRecord` that advances a repo MUST produce a signed Commit. `getHead.commit` is that Commit CID. `data` on the head JSON is the MST root.

The Commit is DAG-CBOR signed with the Solana off-chain envelope (same construction as records). `data` MUST be the new MST root. `prev` MUST be the previous Commit CID, or absent/null at genesis. A client-supplied `prev` that does not equal the current head Commit CID MUST return `ConcurrentHeads` (HTTP 409). `rev` MUST increase; rollback MUST be refused. `getRepo` / import CAR MUST include Commit blocks. Import MUST verify each commit signature and the `prev` chain back to genesis or to `since`. Record-level `prev` (CRDT / Last-ts-wins) is unchanged.

See [Repositories](./07-repositories.md#commit) and [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-repo-putrecord).

## 21.13 Compact `I(C)` retained and verified

**Problem.** Clients accepted a signature-valid compact plus uncovered ops and could not re-check a lying snapshot once `I(C)` blocks were gone.

**Change.** Compact records MUST permanently list `I(C)` as `included`. The authoring knot MUST NOT drop those blocks. `getRepo` / `getBlocks` MUST still serve them. A client MUST reject a compact if any CID in `I(C)` cannot be fetched and verified as a signed page op, or if Apply(`I(C)`) does not equal the snapshot. Stale concurrent ops still merge on top.

See [Data model](./06-data-model.md#compaction).

## 21.14 Subscribe `since` persisted

**Problem.** The subscribe event window lived only in memory and was lost on restart.

**Change.** An online knot MUST persist the commit event log next to the filesystem snapshot. Restart MUST still replay `since` for retained events.

See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#live).

## 21.15 `getRepo ?since=` historical MST

**Problem.** A `since` CAR returned later commits plus the current public records, not the MST snapshots of intermediate commits.

**Change.** `since` MUST return the commit chain after `since` (and the `since` commit block) and the MST nodes plus records needed to reconstruct those commits. Import MUST verify the `prev` chain.

See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#get-repo) and [Repositories](./07-repositories.md#car-export).

## 21.16 ActivityPub RFC 9421 required

**Problem.** Attested JSON `{did, actor}` without HTTP Message Signatures could still pass.

**Change.** ActivityPub `sys.foreign` / `sys.binding` ingest MUST have a verifiable RFC 9421 signature in addition to `attested: true` and `{did, actor}` when those fields apply. Attested-only MUST be rejected.

See [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md#activitypub).

## 21.17 RFC 9421 covered-component set

**Problem.** The verified subset was only `@method` `@path` `content-digest`. Extra covered components were ignored.

**Change.** Implementations MUST implement `@method`, `@path`, `content-digest`, and MUST verify `@authority` (or `host`) and `content-type` when listed in `Signature-Input`. Other RFC 9421 features MAY be ignored.

See [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md#activitypub).

## 21.18 `max_uses` persisted across restart

**Problem.** A forgotten `max_uses` counter reset to zero, so a one-use grant could be reused after restart.

**Change.** An online knot MUST persist the counter in the same snapshot as records. Restart MUST NOT reset counts.

See [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md#caveats).

## 21.19 MLS wrapping vector vs live OpenMLS

**Problem.** `spec/vectors/mls-welcome-commit.json` `payload_hex` is wrapping-only; OpenMLS Welcome bytes are not byte-stable.

**Change.** That file remains the wrapping vector (ciphersuite, exporter label, record shape). Live RFC 9420 bytes are covered by `cargo test -p tangled --lib mls::`. OpenMLS Welcome hex is not frozen (not deterministic).

See [Test vectors](./vectors/README.md).

## 21.20 Public peer gossip on `node.describe`

**Problem.** A knot that knew one other knot had no specified way to learn that peer’s other public knots. There is no DHT.

**Change.** `tangled.node.describe` MAY include `peers`: an array of absolute knot base URLs the operator marked public.

A knot MUST advertise only its operator-configured public set (`--peer`, `TANGLED_PEERS`, or `{data}/peers.txt` in the reference knot). It MUST NOT re-advertise URLs learned from other knots. A connecting knot that successfully describes a peer MAY store that `peers` list and try those URLs for sync and resolve. Omitted `peers` means `[]`. Private or internal knots MUST NOT be listed.

See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-node-describe) and [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#peer-discovery).

## 21.21 Public node statistics

**Problem.** `node.describe` advertises profiles, blob limits, and public peers. Clients had no specified way to read knot-local public counts or hosted-identity topology without walking every `getHead` / `getRepo`.

**Change.** `GET /xrpc/tangled.node.stats` returns public-only aggregates (`counts`, retained public commit `rates`) and advertised-peer topology (`topology.peers`, `topology.hosted`).

A knot MUST count only live `vis: public` tips. It MUST NOT include `cap` / `sealed` records, capability or session counters, or learned peer URLs. `topology.peers` MUST equal `node.describe` `peers`. There is no global directory; clients MAY crawl advertised peers. See [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-node-stats) and [Threat model](./18-threat-model.md#discovery-and-gateways).
